   165→                None
   166→            } else {
   167→                filtered_pathspec = Some(filtered);
   168→                filtered_pathspec.as_ref()
   169→            }
   170→        })
   171→    });
   172→    debug_log(&format!(
   173→        "[BENCHMARK] Pathspec filtering took {:?}",
   174→        pathspec_start.elapsed()
   175→    ));
   176→
   177→    let files_start = Instant::now();
   178→    let files = get_all_tracked_files(
   179→        repo,
   180→        &base_commit,
   181→        &working_log,
   182→        pathspec_filter,
   183→        is_pre_commit,
   184→    )?;
   185→    debug_log(&format!(
   186→        "[BENCHMARK] get_all_tracked_files found {} files, took {:?}",
   187→        files.len(),
   188→        files_start.elapsed()
   189→    ));
   190→
   191→    let read_checkpoints_start = Instant::now();
   192→    let mut checkpoints = if reset {
   193→        // If reset flag is set, start with an empty working log
   194→        working_log.reset_working_log()?;
   195→        Vec::new()
   196→    } else {
   197→        working_log.read_all_checkpoints()?
   198→    };
   199→    debug_log(&format!(
   200→        "[BENCHMARK] Reading {} checkpoints took {:?}",
   201→        checkpoints.len(),
   202→        read_checkpoints_start.elapsed()
   203→    ));
   204→
   205→    if show_working_log {
   206→        if checkpoints.is_empty() {
   207→            debug_log("No working log entries found.");
   208→        } else {
   209→            debug_log("Working Log Entries:");
   210→            debug_log(&format!("{}", "=".repeat(80)));
   211→            for (i, checkpoint) in checkpoints.iter().enumerate() {
   212→                debug_log(&format!("Checkpoint {}", i + 1));
   213→                debug_log(&format!("  Diff: {}", checkpoint.diff));
   214→                debug_log(&format!("  Author: {}", checkpoint.author));
   215→                debug_log(&format!(
   216→                    "  Agent ID: {}",
   217→                    checkpoint
   218→                        .agent_id
   219→                        .as_ref()
   220→                        .map(|id| id.tool.clone())
   221→                        .unwrap_or_default()
   222→                ));
   223→
   224→                // Display first user message from transcript if available
   225→                if let Some(transcript) = &checkpoint.transcript {
   226→                    if let Some(first_message) = transcript.messages().first() {
   227→                        if let crate::authorship::transcript::Message::User { text, .. } =
   228→                            first_message
   229→                        {
   230→                            let agent_info = checkpoint
   231→                                .agent_id
   232→                                .as_ref()
   233→                                .map(|id| format!(" (Agent: {})", id.tool))
   234→                                .unwrap_or_default();
   235→                            let message_count = transcript.messages().len();
   236→                            debug_log(&format!(
   237→                                "  First message{} ({} messages): {}",
   238→                                agent_info, message_count, text
   239→                            ));
   240→                        }
   241→                    }
   242→                }
   243→
   244→                debug_log("  Entries:");
   245→                for entry in &checkpoint.entries {
   246→                    debug_log(&format!("    File: {}", entry.file));
   247→                    debug_log(&format!("    Blob SHA: {}", entry.blob_sha));
   248→                    debug_log(&format!(
   249→                        "    Line Attributions: {:?}",
   250→                        entry.line_attributions
   251→                    ));
   252→                    debug_log(&format!("    Attributions: {:?}", entry.attributions));
   253→                }
   254→                debug_log("");
   255→            }
   256→        }
   257→        return Ok((0, files.len(), checkpoints.len()));
   258→    }
   259→
   260→    // Save current file states and get content hashes
   261→    let save_states_start = Instant::now();
   262→    let file_content_hashes = save_current_file_states(&working_log, &files)?;
   263→    debug_log(&format!(
   264→        "[BENCHMARK] save_current_file_states for {} files took {:?}",
   265→        files.len(),
   266→        save_states_start.elapsed()
   267→    ));
   268→
   269→    // Order file hashes by key and create a hash of the ordered hashes
   270→    let hash_compute_start = Instant::now();
   271→    let mut ordered_hashes: Vec<_> = file_content_hashes.iter().collect();
   272→    ordered_hashes.sort_by_key(|(file_path, _)| *file_path);
   273→
   274→    let mut combined_hasher = Sha256::new();
   275→    for (file_path, hash) in ordered_hashes {
   276→        combined_hasher.update(file_path.as_bytes());
   277→        combined_hasher.update(hash.as_bytes());
   278→    }
   279→    let combined_hash = format!("{:x}", combined_hasher.finalize());
   280→    debug_log(&format!(
   281→        "[BENCHMARK] Hash computation took {:?}",
   282→        hash_compute_start.elapsed()
   283→    ));
   284→
   285→    // Note: foreign prompts from INITIAL file are read in post_commit.rs
   286→    // when converting working log -> authorship log
   287→
   288→    // Get checkpoint entries using unified function that handles both initial and subsequent checkpoints
   289→    let entries_start = Instant::now();
   290→    let (entries, file_stats) = smol::block_on(get_checkpoint_entries(
   291→        kind,
   292→        repo,
   293→        &working_log,
   294→        &files,
   295→        &file_content_hashes,
   296→        &checkpoints,
   297→        agent_run_result.as_ref(),
   298→        ts,
   299→    ))?;
   300→    debug_log(&format!(
   301→        "[BENCHMARK] get_checkpoint_entries generated {} entries, took {:?}",
   302→        entries.len(),
   303→        entries_start.elapsed()
   304→    ));
   305→
   306→    // Skip adding checkpoint if there are no changes
   307→    if !entries.is_empty() {
   308→        let checkpoint_create_start = Instant::now();
   309→        let mut checkpoint = Checkpoint::new(
   310→            kind.clone(),
   311→            combined_hash.clone(),
   312→            author.to_string(),
   313→            entries.clone(),
   314→        );
   315→
   316→        // Aggregate line stats from in-memory stats (computed during entry creation)
   317→        checkpoint.line_stats = compute_line_stats(&file_stats)?;
   318→
   319→        // Set transcript and agent_id if provided and not a human checkpoint
   320→        if kind != CheckpointKind::Human
   321→            && let Some(agent_run) = &agent_run_result
   322→        {
   323→            checkpoint.transcript = Some(agent_run.transcript.clone().unwrap_or_default());
   324→            checkpoint.agent_id = Some(agent_run.agent_id.clone());
   325→            checkpoint.agent_metadata = agent_run.agent_metadata.clone();
   326→        }
   327→        debug_log(&format!(
   328→            "[BENCHMARK] Checkpoint creation took {:?}",
   329→            checkpoint_create_start.elapsed()
   330→        ));
   331→
   332→        // Upsert prompt to database (non-fatal if it fails)
   333→        if kind != CheckpointKind::Human && checkpoint.agent_id.is_some() {
   334→            if checkpoint.transcript.is_some() {
   335→                if let Err(e) = upsert_checkpoint_prompt_to_db(
   336→                    &checkpoint,
   337→                    working_log.repo_workdir.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
   338→                    None, // commit_sha is None at checkpoint stage
   339→                ) {
   340→                    debug_log(&format!(
   341→                        "[Warning] Failed to upsert prompt to database: {}",
   342→                        e
   343→                    ));
   344→                    crate::observability::log_error(
   345→                        &e,
   346→                        Some(serde_json::json!({
   347→                            "operation": "checkpoint_prompt_upsert",
   348→                            "agent_tool": checkpoint.agent_id.as_ref().map(|a| a.tool.as_str())
   349→                        })),
   350→                    );
   351→                }
   352→            }
   353→        }
   354→
   355→        // Append checkpoint to the working log
   356→        let append_start = Instant::now();
   357→        working_log.append_checkpoint(&checkpoint)?;
   358→        debug_log(&format!(
   359→            "[BENCHMARK] Appending checkpoint to working log took {:?}",
   360→            append_start.elapsed()
   361→        ));
   362→        checkpoints.push(checkpoint.clone());
   363→
   364→        // Record agent usage metric for AI checkpoints
   365→        if kind != CheckpointKind::Human {
   366→            if let Some(agent_id) = &checkpoint.agent_id {
   367→                let prompt_id = generate_short_hash(&agent_id.id, &agent_id.tool);
   368→
   369→                let values = crate::metrics::AgentUsageValues::new();
   370→                let mut attrs = crate::metrics::EventAttributes::with_version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
   371→                    .tool(&agent_id.tool)
   372→                    .model(&agent_id.model)
   373→                    .prompt_id(prompt_id)
   374→                    .external_prompt_id(&agent_id.id);
   375→
   376→                // Get repo URL from default remote
   377→                if let Ok(Some(remote_name)) = repo.get_default_remote() {
   378→                    if let Ok(remotes) = repo.remotes_with_urls() {
   379→                        if let Some((_, url)) = remotes.into_iter().find(|(n, _)| n == &remote_name) {
   380→                            if let Ok(normalized) = crate::repo_url::normalize_repo_url(&url) {
   381→                                attrs = attrs.repo_url(normalized);
   382→                            }
   383→                        }
   384→                    }
   385→                }
   386→
   387→                crate::metrics::record(values, attrs);
   388→            }
   389→        }
   390→    }
   391→
   392→    let agent_tool = if kind != CheckpointKind::Human
   393→        && let Some(agent_run_result) = &agent_run_result
   394→    {
   395→        Some(agent_run_result.agent_id.tool.as_str())
   396→    } else {
   397→        None
   398→    };
   399→
   400→    // Print summary with new format
   401→    if reset {
   402→        debug_log("Working log reset. Starting fresh checkpoint.");
   403→    }
   404→
   405→    let label = if entries.len() > 1 {
   406→        "checkpoint"
   407→    } else {
   408→        "commit"
   409→    };
   410→
   411→    if !quiet {
   412→        let log_author = agent_tool.unwrap_or(author);
   413→        // Only count files that actually have checkpoint entries to avoid confusion.
   414→        // Files that were previously checkpointed but have no new changes won't have entries.
   415→        let files_with_entries = entries.len();
   416→        let total_uncommitted_files = files.len();
   417→
   418→        if files_with_entries == total_uncommitted_files {
   419→            // All files with changes got entries
   420→            eprintln!(
   421→                "{} {} changed {} file(s) that have changed since the last {}",
   422→                kind.to_str(),
   423→                log_author,
   424→                files_with_entries,
   425→                label
   426→            );
   427→        } else {
   428→            // Some files were already checkpointed
   429→            eprintln!(
   430→                "{} {} changed {} of the {} file(s) that have changed since the last {} ({} already checkpointed)",
   431→                kind.to_str(),
   432→                log_author,
   433→                files_with_entries,
   434→                total_uncommitted_files,
   435→                label,
   436→                total_uncommitted_files - files_with_entries
   437→            );
   438→        }
   439→    }
   440→
   441→    // Return the requested values: (entries_len, files_len, working_log_len)
   442→    debug_log(&format!(
   443→        "[BENCHMARK] Total checkpoint run took {:?}",
   444→        checkpoint_start.elapsed()
   445→    ));
   446→    Ok((entries.len(), files.len(), checkpoints.len()))
   447→}
   448→
   449→// Gets tracked changes AND
   450→fn get_status_of_files(
   451→    repo: &Repository,
   452→    working_log: &PersistedWorkingLog,
   453→    edited_filepaths: HashSet<String>,
   454→    skip_untracked: bool,
   455→) -> Result<Vec<String>, GitAiError> {
   456→    let mut files = Vec::new();
   457→
   458→    // Use porcelain v2 format to get status
   459→
   460→    let edited_filepaths_option = if edited_filepaths.is_empty() {
   461→        None
   462→    } else {
   463→        Some(&edited_filepaths)
   464→    };
   465→
   466→    let status_start = Instant::now();
   467→    let statuses = repo.status(edited_filepaths_option, skip_untracked)?;
   468→    debug_log(&format!(
   469→        "[BENCHMARK]   git status call took {:?}",
   470→        status_start.elapsed()
   471→    ));
   472→
   473→    for entry in statuses {
   474→        // Skip ignored files
   475→        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Ignored {
   476→            continue;
   477→        }
   478→
   479→        // Skip unmerged/conflicted files - we'll track them once the conflict is resolved
   480→        if entry.kind == EntryKind::Unmerged {
   481→            continue;
   482→        }
   483→
   484→        // Include files that have any change (staged or unstaged) or are untracked
   485→        let has_change = entry.staged != StatusCode::Unmodified
   486→            || entry.unstaged != StatusCode::Unmodified
   487→            || entry.kind == EntryKind::Untracked;
   488→
   489→        if has_change {
   490→            // For deleted files, check if they were text files in HEAD
   491→            let is_deleted =
   492→                entry.staged == StatusCode::Deleted || entry.unstaged == StatusCode::Deleted;
   493→
   494→            let is_text = if is_deleted {
   495→                is_text_file_in_head(repo, &entry.path)
   496→            } else {
   497→                is_text_file(working_log, &entry.path)
   498→            };
   499→
   500→            if is_text {
   501→                files.push(entry.path.clone());
   502→            }
   503→        }
   504→    }
   505→
   506→    Ok(files)
   507→}
   508→
   509→/// Get all files that should be tracked, including those from previous checkpoints and INITIAL attributions
   510→///
   511→fn get_all_tracked_files(
   512→    repo: &Repository,
   513→    _base_commit: &str,
   514→    working_log: &PersistedWorkingLog,
   515→    edited_filepaths: Option<&Vec<String>>,
   516→    is_pre_commit: bool,
   517→) -> Result<Vec<String>, GitAiError> {
   518→    let mut files: HashSet<String> = edited_filepaths
   519→        .map(|paths| paths.iter().cloned().collect())
   520→        .unwrap_or_default();
   521→
   522→    let initial_read_start = Instant::now();
   523→    for file in working_log.read_initial_attributions().files.keys() {
   524→        // Normalize path separators to forward slashes
   525→        let normalized_path = normalize_to_posix(file);
   526→        if is_text_file(working_log, &normalized_path) {
   527→            files.insert(normalized_path);
   528→        }
   529→    }
   530→    debug_log(&format!(
   531→        "[BENCHMARK]   Reading INITIAL attributions in get_all_tracked_files took {:?}",
   532→        initial_read_start.elapsed()
   533→    ));
   534→
   535→    let checkpoints_read_start = Instant::now();
   536→    if let Ok(working_log_data) = working_log.read_all_checkpoints() {
   537→        for checkpoint in &working_log_data {
   538→            for entry in &checkpoint.entries {
   539→                // Normalize path separators to forward slashes
   540→                let normalized_path = normalize_to_posix(&entry.file);
   541→                if !files.contains(&normalized_path) {
   542→                    // Check if it's a text file before adding
   543→                    if is_text_file(working_log, &normalized_path) {
   544→                        files.insert(normalized_path);
   545→                    }
   546→                }
   547→            }
   548→        }
   549→    }
   550→    debug_log(&format!(
   551→        "[BENCHMARK]   Reading checkpoints in get_all_tracked_files took {:?}",
   552→        checkpoints_read_start.elapsed()
   553→    ));
   554→
   555→    let has_ai_checkpoints = if let Ok(working_log_data) = working_log.read_all_checkpoints() {
   556→        working_log_data.iter().any(|checkpoint| {
   557→            checkpoint.kind == CheckpointKind::AiAgent || checkpoint.kind == CheckpointKind::AiTab
   558→        })
   559→    } else {
   560→        false
   561→    };
   562→
   563→    let status_files_start = Instant::now();
   564→    let mut results_for_tracked_files = if is_pre_commit && !has_ai_checkpoints {
   565→        get_status_of_files(repo, working_log, files, true)?
   566→    } else {
   567→        get_status_of_files(repo, working_log, files, false)?
   568→    };
   569→    debug_log(&format!(
   570→        "[BENCHMARK]   get_status_of_files in get_all_tracked_files took {:?}",
   571→        status_files_start.elapsed()
   572→    ));
   573→
   574→    // Ensure to always include all dirty files
   575→    if let Some(ref dirty_files) = working_log.dirty_files {
   576→        for file_path in dirty_files.keys() {
   577→            // Normalize path separators to forward slashes
   578→            let normalized_path = normalize_to_posix(file_path);
   579→            // Only add if not already in the files list
   580→            if !results_for_tracked_files.contains(&normalized_path) {
   581→                // Check if it's a text file before adding
   582→                if is_text_file(working_log, &normalized_path) {
   583→                    results_for_tracked_files.push(normalized_path);
   584→                }
   585→            }
   586→        }
   587→    }
   588→
   589→    Ok(results_for_tracked_files)
   590→}
   591→
   592→fn save_current_file_states(
   593→    working_log: &PersistedWorkingLog,
   594→    files: &[String],
   595→) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, GitAiError> {
   596→    let read_start = Instant::now();
   597→
   598→    // Extract only the data we need (no cloning the entire working_log)
   599→    let blobs_dir = working_log.dir.join("blobs");
   600→    let repo_workdir = working_log.repo_workdir.clone();
   601→    let dirty_files = working_log.dirty_files.clone();
   602→
   603→    // Process files concurrently with a semaphore limiting to 8 at a time
   604→    let file_content_hashes = smol::block_on(async {
   605→        let semaphore = Arc::new(smol::lock::Semaphore::new(8));
   606→        let blobs_dir = Arc::new(blobs_dir);
   607→        let repo_workdir = Arc::new(repo_workdir);
   608→        let dirty_files = Arc::new(dirty_files);
   609→
   610→        let futures = files.iter().map(|file_path| {
   611→            let file_path = file_path.clone();
   612→            let blobs_dir = Arc::clone(&blobs_dir);
   613→            let repo_workdir = Arc::clone(&repo_workdir);
   614→            let dirty_files = Arc::clone(&dirty_files);
   615→            let semaphore = Arc::clone(&semaphore);
   616→
   617→            async move {
   618→                // Acquire semaphore permit
   619→                let _permit = semaphore.acquire().await;
   620→
   621→                // Read file content - check dirty_files first, then filesystem
   622→                let content = if let Some(ref dirty_map) = *dirty_files {
   623→                    dirty_map.get(&file_path).cloned()
   624→                } else {
   625→                    None
   626→                }
   627→                .unwrap_or_else(|| {
   628→                    // Construct absolute path
   629→                    let abs_path = if std::path::Path::new(&file_path).is_absolute() {
   630→                        file_path.clone()
   631→                    } else {
   632→                        repo_workdir.join(&file_path).to_string_lossy().to_string()
   633→                    };
   634→                    // Read from filesystem
   635→                    std::fs::read_to_string(&abs_path).unwrap_or_default()
   636→                });
   637→
   638→                // Create SHA256 hash of the content
   639→                let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
   640→                hasher.update(content.as_bytes());
   641→                let sha = format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize());
   642→
   643→                // Ensure blobs directory exists
   644→                std::fs::create_dir_all(&*blobs_dir)?;
   645→
   646→                // Write content to blob file
   647→                let blob_path = blobs_dir.join(&sha);
   648→                std::fs::write(blob_path, content)?;
   649→
   650→                Ok::<(String, String), GitAiError>((file_path, sha))
   651→            }
   652→        });
   653→
   654→        // Collect results from all concurrent operations
   655→        let results: Vec<Result<(String, String), GitAiError>> =
   656→            stream::iter(futures).buffer_unordered(8).collect().await;
   657→
   658→        // Convert results into HashMap
   659→        let mut file_content_hashes = HashMap::new();
   660→        for result in results {
   661→            let (file_path, content_hash) = result?;
   662→            file_content_hashes.insert(file_path, content_hash);
   663→        }
   664→
   665→        Ok::<HashMap<String, String>, GitAiError>(file_content_hashes)
   666→    })?;
   667→
   668→    Ok(file_content_hashes)
   669→}
   670→
   671→fn get_checkpoint_entry_for_file(
   672→    file_path: String,
   673→    kind: CheckpointKind,
   674→    repo: Repository,
   675→    working_log: PersistedWorkingLog,
   676→    previous_checkpoints: Arc<Vec<Checkpoint>>,
   677→    file_content_hash: String,
   678→    author_id: Arc<String>,
   679→    head_commit_sha: Arc<Option<String>>,
   680→    head_tree_id: Arc<Option<String>>,
   681→    initial_attributions: Arc<HashMap<String, Vec<LineAttribution>>>,
   682→    ts: u128,
   683→) -> Result<Option<(WorkingLogEntry, FileLineStats)>, GitAiError> {
   684→    let feature_flag_inter_commit_move = Config::get().get_feature_flags().inter_commit_move;
   685→
   686→    let file_start = Instant::now();
   687→    let current_content = working_log
   688→        .read_current_file_content(&file_path)
   689→        .unwrap_or_default();
   690→
   691→    // Try to get previous state from checkpoints first
   692→    let from_checkpoint = previous_checkpoints.iter().rev().find_map(|checkpoint| {
   693→        checkpoint
   694→            .entries
   695→            .iter()
   696→            .find(|e| e.file == file_path)
   697→            .map(|entry| {
   698→                (
   699→                    working_log
   700→                        .get_file_version(&entry.blob_sha)
   701→                        .unwrap_or_default(),
   702→                    entry.attributions.clone(),
   703→                )
   704→            })
   705→    });
   706→
   707→    // Get INITIAL attributions for this file (needed early for the skip check)
   708→    let initial_attrs_for_file = initial_attributions
   709→        .get(&file_path)
   710→        .cloned()
   711→        .unwrap_or_default();
   712→
   713→    let is_from_checkpoint = from_checkpoint.is_some();
   714→    let (previous_content, prev_attributions) = if let Some((content, attrs)) = from_checkpoint {
   715→        // File exists in a previous checkpoint - use that
   716→        (content, attrs)
   717→    } else {
   718→        // File doesn't exist in any previous checkpoint - need to initialize from git + INITIAL
   719→        // Get previous content from HEAD tree
   720→        let previous_content = if let Some(tree_id) = head_tree_id.as_ref().as_ref() {
   721→            let head_tree = repo.find_tree(tree_id.clone()).ok();
   722→            if let Some(tree) = head_tree {
   723→                match tree.get_path(std::path::Path::new(&file_path)) {
   724→                    Ok(entry) => {
   725→                        if let Ok(blob) = repo.find_blob(entry.id()) {
   726→                            let blob_content = blob.content().unwrap_or_default();
   727→                            String::from_utf8_lossy(&blob_content).to_string()
   728→                        } else {
   729→                            String::new()
   730→                        }
   731→                    }
   732→                    Err(_) => String::new(),
   733→                }
   734→            } else {
   735→                String::new()
   736→            }
   737→        } else {
   738→            String::new()
   739→        };
   740→
   741→        // Skip if no changes, UNLESS we have INITIAL attributions for this file
   742→        // (in which case we need to create an entry to record those attributions)
   743→        if current_content == previous_content && initial_attrs_for_file.is_empty() {
   744→            return Ok(None);
   745→        }
   746→
   747→        // Build a set of lines covered by INITIAL attributions
   748→        let mut initial_covered_lines: HashSet<u32> = HashSet::new();
   749→        for attr in &initial_attrs_for_file {
   750→            for line in attr.start_line..=attr.end_line {
   751→                initial_covered_lines.insert(line);
   752→            }
   753→        }
   754→
   755→        // Start with INITIAL attributions (they win)
   756→        let mut prev_line_attributions = initial_attrs_for_file.clone();
   757→        let mut blamed_lines: HashSet<u32> = HashSet::new();
   758→
   759→        // Get blame for lines not in INITIAL
   760→        let blame_start = Instant::now();
   761→        let mut ai_blame_opts = GitAiBlameOptions::default();
   762→        ai_blame_opts.no_output = true;
   763→        ai_blame_opts.return_human_authors_as_human = true;
   764→        ai_blame_opts.use_prompt_hashes_as_names = true;
   765→        ai_blame_opts.newest_commit = head_commit_sha.as_ref().clone();
   766→        ai_blame_opts.oldest_date = Some(OLDEST_AI_BLAME_DATE.clone());
   767→        let ai_blame = if feature_flag_inter_commit_move {
   768→            repo.blame(&file_path, &ai_blame_opts).ok()
   769→        } else {
   770→            // When skipping blame, default all lines to "human"
   771→            let total_lines = previous_content.lines().count() as u32;
   772→            let mut line_authors: HashMap<u32, String> = HashMap::new();
   773→            for line_num in 1..=total_lines {
   774→                line_authors.insert(line_num, CheckpointKind::Human.to_str());
   775→            }
   776→            let prompt_records: HashMap<String, PromptRecord> = HashMap::new();
   777→            Some((line_authors, prompt_records))
   778→        };
   779→
   780→        debug_log(&format!(
   781→            "[BENCHMARK] Blame for {} took {:?}",
   782→            file_path,
   783→            blame_start.elapsed()
   784→        ));
   785→
   786→        // Add blame results for lines NOT covered by INITIAL
   787→        if let Some((blames, _)) = ai_blame {
   788→            for (line, author) in blames {
   789→                blamed_lines.insert(line);
   790→                // Skip if INITIAL already has this line
   791→                if initial_covered_lines.contains(&line) {
   792→                    continue;
   793→                }
   794→
   795→                // Skip human-authored lines - they should remain human
   796→                if author == CheckpointKind::Human.to_str() {
   797→                    continue;
   798→                }
   799→
   800→                prev_line_attributions.push(LineAttribution {
   801→                    start_line: line,
   802→                    end_line: line,
   803→                    author_id: author.clone(),
   804→                    overrode: None,
   805→                });
   806→            }
   807→        }
   808→
   809→        // For AI checkpoints, attribute any lines NOT in INITIAL and NOT returned by ai_blame
   810→        if kind != CheckpointKind::Human {
   811→            let total_lines = current_content.lines().count() as u32;
   812→            for line_num in 1..=total_lines {
   813→                if !initial_covered_lines.contains(&line_num) && !blamed_lines.contains(&line_num) {
   814→                    prev_line_attributions.push(LineAttribution {
   815→                        start_line: line_num,
   816→                        end_line: line_num,
   817→                        author_id: author_id.as_ref().clone(),
   818→                        overrode: None,
   819→                    });
   820→                }
   821→            }
   822→        }
   823→
   824→        // For INITIAL attributions, we need to use current_content (not previous_content)
   825→        // because INITIAL line numbers refer to the current state of the file
   826→        let content_for_line_conversion = if !initial_attrs_for_file.is_empty() {
   827→            &current_content
   828→        } else {
   829→            &previous_content
   830→        };
   831→
   832→        // Convert any line attributions to character attributions
   833→        let prev_attributions =
   834→            crate::authorship::attribution_tracker::line_attributions_to_attributions(
   835→                &prev_line_attributions,
   836→                content_for_line_conversion,
   837→                INITIAL_ATTRIBUTION_TS,
   838→            );
   839→
   840→        // When we have INITIAL attributions, they describe the current state of the file.
   841→        // We need to pass current_content as previous_content so the attributions are preserved.
   842→        // The tracker will see no changes and preserve the INITIAL attributions.
   843→        let adjusted_previous = if !initial_attrs_for_file.is_empty() {
   844→            current_content.clone()
   845→        } else {
   846→            previous_content
   847→        };
   848→
   849→        (adjusted_previous, prev_attributions)
   850→    };
   851→
   852→    // Skip if no changes (but we already checked this earlier, accounting for INITIAL attributions)
   853→    // For files from previous checkpoints, check if content has changed
   854→    if is_from_checkpoint && current_content == previous_content {
   855→        return Ok(None);
   856→    }
   857→
   858→    let (entry, stats) = make_entry_for_file(
   859→        &file_path,
   860→        &file_content_hash,
   861→        author_id.as_ref(),
   862→        &previous_content,
   863→        &prev_attributions,
   864→        &current_content,
   865→        ts,
   866→    )?;
   867→    debug_log(&format!(
   868→        "[BENCHMARK] Processing file {} took {:?}",
   869→        file_path,
   870→        file_start.elapsed()
   871→    ));
   872→    Ok(Some((entry, stats)))
   873→}
   874→
   875→async fn get_checkpoint_entries(
   876→    kind: CheckpointKind,
   877→    repo: &Repository,
   878→    working_log: &PersistedWorkingLog,
   879→    files: &[String],
   880→    file_content_hashes: &HashMap<String, String>,
   881→    previous_checkpoints: &[Checkpoint],
   882→    agent_run_result: Option<&AgentRunResult>,
   883→    ts: u128,
   884→) -> Result<(Vec<WorkingLogEntry>, Vec<FileLineStats>), GitAiError> {
   885→    let entries_fn_start = Instant::now();
   886→
   887→    // Read INITIAL attributions from working log (empty if file doesn't exist)
   888→    let initial_read_start = Instant::now();
   889→    let initial_data = working_log.read_initial_attributions();
   890→    let initial_attributions = initial_data.files;
   891→    debug_log(&format!(
   892→        "[BENCHMARK] Reading initial attributions took {:?}",
   893→        initial_read_start.elapsed()
   894→    ));
   895→
   896→    // Determine author_id based on checkpoint kind and agent_id
   897→    let author_id = if kind != CheckpointKind::Human {
   898→        // For AI checkpoints, use session hash
   899→        agent_run_result
   900→            .map(|result| {
   901→                crate::authorship::authorship_log_serialization::generate_short_hash(
   902→                    &result.agent_id.id,
   903→                    &result.agent_id.tool,
   904→                )
   905→            })
   906→            .unwrap_or_else(|| kind.to_str())
   907→    } else {
   908→        // For human checkpoints, use checkpoint kind string
   909→        kind.to_str()
   910→    };
   911→
   912→    // Get HEAD commit info for git operations
   913→    let head_commit = repo
   914→        .head()
   915→        .ok()
   916→        .and_then(|h| h.target().ok())
   917→        .and_then(|oid| repo.find_commit(oid).ok());
   918→    let head_commit_sha = head_commit.as_ref().map(|c| c.id().to_string());
   919→    let head_tree_id = head_commit
   920→        .as_ref()
   921→        .and_then(|c| c.tree().ok())
   922→        .map(|t| t.id().to_string());
   923→
   924→    const MAX_CONCURRENT: usize = 30;
   925→
   926→    // Create a semaphore to limit concurrent tasks
   927→    let semaphore = Arc::new(smol::lock::Semaphore::new(MAX_CONCURRENT));
   928→
   929→    // Move checkpoint data to Arc once, outside the loop to avoid repeated allocations
   930→    let previous_checkpoints = Arc::new(previous_checkpoints.to_vec());
   931→
   932→    // Move other repeated allocations outside the loop
   933→    let author_id = Arc::new(author_id);
   934→    let head_commit_sha = Arc::new(head_commit_sha);
   935→    let head_tree_id = Arc::new(head_tree_id);
   936→    let initial_attributions = Arc::new(initial_attributions);
   937→
   938→    // Spawn tasks for each file
   939→    let spawn_start = Instant::now();
   940→    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
   941→
   942→    for file_path in files {
   943→        let file_path = file_path.clone();
   944→        let repo = repo.clone();
   945→        let working_log = working_log.clone();
   946→        let previous_checkpoints = Arc::clone(&previous_checkpoints);
   947→        let author_id = Arc::clone(&author_id);
   948→        let head_commit_sha = Arc::clone(&head_commit_sha);
   949→        let head_tree_id = Arc::clone(&head_tree_id);
   950→        let blob_sha = file_content_hashes
   951→            .get(&file_path)
   952→            .cloned()
   953→            .unwrap_or_default();
   954→        let initial_attributions = Arc::clone(&initial_attributions);
   955→        let semaphore = Arc::clone(&semaphore);
   956→        let kind = kind.clone();
   957→
   958→        let task = smol::spawn(async move {
   959→            // Acquire semaphore permit to limit concurrency
   960→            let _permit = semaphore.acquire().await;
   961→
   962→            // Wrap all the blocking git operations in smol::unblock
   963→            smol::unblock(move || {
   964→                get_checkpoint_entry_for_file(
   965→                    file_path,
   966→                    kind,
   967→                    repo,
   968→                    working_log,
   969→                    previous_checkpoints,
   970→                    blob_sha,
   971→                    author_id.clone(),
   972→                    head_commit_sha.clone(),
   973→                    head_tree_id.clone(),
   974→                    initial_attributions.clone(),
   975→                    ts,
   976→                )
   977→            })
   978→            .await
   979→        });
   980→
   981→        tasks.push(task);
   982→    }
   983→    debug_log(&format!(
   984→        "[BENCHMARK] Spawning {} tasks took {:?}",
   985→        tasks.len(),
   986→        spawn_start.elapsed()
   987→    ));
   988→
   989→    // Await all tasks concurrently
   990→    let await_start = Instant::now();
   991→    let results = futures::future::join_all(tasks).await;
   992→    debug_log(&format!(
   993→        "[BENCHMARK] Awaiting {} tasks took {:?}",
   994→        results.len(),
   995→        await_start.elapsed()
   996→    ));
   997→
   998→    // Process results
   999→    let process_start = Instant::now();
  1000→    let results_count = results.len();
  1001→    let mut entries = Vec::new();
  1002→    let mut file_stats = Vec::new();
  1003→    for result in results {
  1004→        match result {
  1005→            Ok(Some((entry, stats))) => {
  1006→                entries.push(entry);
  1007→                file_stats.push(stats);
  1008→            }
  1009→            Ok(None) => {} // File had no changes
  1010→            Err(e) => return Err(e),
  1011→        }
  1012→    }
  1013→    debug_log(&format!(
  1014→        "[BENCHMARK] Processing {} results took {:?}",
  1015→        results_count,
  1016→        process_start.elapsed()
  1017→    ));
  1018→    debug_log(&format!(
  1019→        "[BENCHMARK] get_checkpoint_entries function total took {:?}",
  1020→        entries_fn_start.elapsed()
  1021→    ));
  1022→
  1023→    Ok((entries, file_stats))
  1024→}
  1025→
  1026→fn make_entry_for_file(
  1027→    file_path: &str,
  1028→    blob_sha: &str,
  1029→    author_id: &str,
  1030→    previous_content: &str,
  1031→    previous_attributions: &Vec<Attribution>,
  1032→    content: &str,
  1033→    ts: u128,
  1034→) -> Result<(WorkingLogEntry, FileLineStats), GitAiError> {
  1035→    let tracker = AttributionTracker::new();
  1036→
  1037→    let fill_start = Instant::now();
  1038→    let filled_in_prev_attributions = tracker.attribute_unattributed_ranges(
  1039→        previous_content,
  1040→        previous_attributions,
  1041→        &CheckpointKind::Human.to_str(),
  1042→        ts - 1,
  1043→    );
  1044→    debug_log(&format!(
  1045→        "[BENCHMARK]   attribute_unattributed_ranges for {} took {:?}",
  1046→        file_path,
  1047→        fill_start.elapsed()
  1048→    ));
  1049→
  1050→    let update_start = Instant::now();
  1051→    let new_attributions = tracker.update_attributions(
  1052→        previous_content,
  1053→        content,
  1054→        &filled_in_prev_attributions,
  1055→        author_id,
  1056→        ts,
  1057→    )?;
  1058→    debug_log(&format!(
  1059→        "[BENCHMARK]   update_attributions for {} took {:?}",
  1060→        file_path,
  1061→        update_start.elapsed()
  1062→    ));
  1063→
  1064→    // TODO Consider discarding any "uncontentious" attributions for the human author. Any human attributions that do not share a line with any other author's attributions can be discarded.
  1065→    // let filtered_attributions = crate::authorship::attribution_tracker::discard_uncontentious_attributions_for_author(&new_attributions, &CheckpointKind::Human.to_str());
  1066→
  1067→    let line_attr_start = Instant::now();
  1068→    let line_attributions =
  1069→        crate::authorship::attribution_tracker::attributions_to_line_attributions(
  1070→            &new_attributions,
  1071→            content,
  1072→        );
  1073→    debug_log(&format!(
  1074→        "[BENCHMARK]   attributions_to_line_attributions for {} took {:?}",
  1075→        file_path,
  1076→        line_attr_start.elapsed()
  1077→    ));
  1078→
  1079→    // Compute line stats while we already have both contents in memory
  1080→    let stats_start = Instant::now();
  1081→    let line_stats = compute_file_line_stats(previous_content, content);
  1082→    debug_log(&format!(
  1083→        "[BENCHMARK]   compute_file_line_stats for {} took {:?}",
  1084→        file_path,
  1085→        stats_start.elapsed()
  1086→    ));
  1087→
  1088→    let entry = WorkingLogEntry::new(
  1089→        file_path.to_string(),
  1090→        blob_sha.to_string(),
  1091→        new_attributions,
  1092→        line_attributions,
  1093→    );
  1094→
  1095→    Ok((entry, line_stats))
  1096→}
  1097→
  1098→/// Compute line statistics for a single file by diffing previous and current content
  1099→fn compute_file_line_stats(previous_content: &str, current_content: &str) -> FileLineStats {
  1100→    let mut stats = FileLineStats::default();
  1101→
  1102→    // Use imara_diff to count line changes (matches git's diff algorithm)
  1103→    let changes = compute_line_changes(previous_content, current_content);
  1104→    for change in changes {
  1105→        match change.tag() {
  1106→            LineChangeTag::Insert => {
  1107→                let non_whitespace_lines = change
  1108→                    .value()
  1109→                    .lines()
  1110→                    .filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
  1111→                    .count() as u32;
  1112→                stats.additions += change.value().lines().count() as u32;
  1113→                stats.additions_sloc += non_whitespace_lines;
  1114→            }
  1115→            LineChangeTag::Delete => {
  1116→                let non_whitespace_lines = change
  1117→                    .value()
  1118→                    .lines()
  1119→                    .filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())
  1120→                    .count() as u32;
  1121→                stats.deletions += change.value().lines().count() as u32;
  1122→                stats.deletions_sloc += non_whitespace_lines;
  1123→            }
  1124→            LineChangeTag::Equal => {}
  1125→        }
  1126→    }
  1127→
  1128→    stats
  1129→}
  1130→
  1131→/// Aggregate line statistics from individual file stats
  1132→/// This avoids redundant diff computation since stats are already computed during entry creation
  1133→fn compute_line_stats(
  1134→    file_stats: &[FileLineStats],
  1135→) -> Result<crate::authorship::working_log::CheckpointLineStats, GitAiError> {
  1136→    let mut stats = crate::authorship::working_log::CheckpointLineStats::default();
  1137→
  1138→    // Aggregate line stats from all files
  1139→    for file_stat in file_stats {
  1140→        stats.additions += file_stat.additions;
  1141→        stats.deletions += file_stat.deletions;
  1142→        stats.additions_sloc += file_stat.additions_sloc;
  1143→        stats.deletions_sloc += file_stat.deletions_sloc;
  1144→    }
  1145→
  1146→    Ok(stats)
  1147→}

  1149→#[cfg(test)]
  1150→mod tests {
  1151→    use super::*;
  1152→    use crate::git::test_utils::TmpRepo;
  1153→
  1154→    #[test]
  1155→    fn test_checkpoint_with_staged_changes() {
  1156→        // Create a repo with an initial commit
  1157→        let (tmp_repo, mut file, _) = TmpRepo::new_with_base_commit().unwrap();
  1158→
  1159→        // Make changes to the file
  1160→        file.append("New line added by user\n").unwrap();
  1161→
  1162→        // Note: TmpFile.append() automatically stages changes (see write_to_disk in test_utils)
  1163→        // So at this point, the file has staged changes
  1164→
  1165→        // Run checkpoint - it should track the changes even though they're staged
  1166→        let (entries_len, files_len, _checkpoints_len) =
  1167→            tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("Aidan").unwrap();
  1168→
  1169→        // The bug: when changes are staged, entries_len is 0 instead of 1
  1170→        assert_eq!(files_len, 1, "Should have 1 file with changes");
  1171→        assert_eq!(
  1172→            entries_len, 1,
  1173→            "Should have 1 file entry in checkpoint (staged changes should be tracked)"
  1174→        );
  1175→    }
  1176→
  1177→    #[test]
  1178→    fn test_checkpoint_with_staged_changes_after_previous_checkpoint() {
  1179→        // Create a repo with an initial commit
  1180→        let (tmp_repo, mut file, _) = TmpRepo::new_with_base_commit().unwrap();
  1181→
  1182→        // Make first changes and checkpoint
  1183→        file.append("First change\n").unwrap();
  1184→        let (entries_len_1, files_len_1, _) =
  1185→            tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("Aidan").unwrap();
  1186→
  1187→        assert_eq!(
  1188→            files_len_1, 1,
  1189→            "First checkpoint: should have 1 file with changes"
  1190→        );
  1191→        assert_eq!(
  1192→            entries_len_1, 1,
  1193→            "First checkpoint: should have 1 file entry"
  1194→        );
  1195→
  1196→        // Make second changes - these are already staged by append()
  1197→        file.append("Second change\n").unwrap();
  1198→
  1199→        // Run checkpoint again - it should track the staged changes even after a previous checkpoint
  1200→        let (entries_len_2, files_len_2, _) =
  1201→            tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("Aidan").unwrap();
  1202→
  1203→        assert_eq!(
  1204→            files_len_2, 1,
  1205→            "Second checkpoint: should have 1 file with changes"
  1206→        );
  1207→        assert_eq!(
  1208→            entries_len_2, 1,
  1209→            "Second checkpoint: should have 1 file entry in checkpoint (staged changes should be tracked)"
  1210→        );
  1211→    }
  1212→
  1213→    #[test]
  1214→    fn test_checkpoint_with_only_staged_no_unstaged_changes() {
  1215→        use std::fs;
  1216→
  1217→        // Create a repo with an initial commit
  1218→        let (tmp_repo, file, _) = TmpRepo::new_with_base_commit().unwrap();
  1219→
  1220→        // Get the file path
  1221→        let file_path = file.path();
  1222→        let filename = file.filename();
  1223→
  1224→        // Manually modify the file (bypassing TmpFile's automatic staging)
  1225→        let mut content = fs::read_to_string(&file_path).unwrap();
  1226→        content.push_str("New line for staging test\n");
  1227→        fs::write(&file_path, &content).unwrap();
  1228→
  1229→        // Now manually stage it using git (this is what "git add" does)
  1230→        tmp_repo.stage_file(filename).unwrap();
  1231→
  1232→        // At this point: HEAD has old content, index has new content, workdir has new content
  1233→        // And unstaged should be "Unmodified" because workdir == index
  1234→
  1235→        // Now run checkpoint
  1236→        let (entries_len, files_len, _checkpoints_len) =
  1237→            tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("Aidan").unwrap();
  1238→
  1239→        // This should work: we should see 1 file with 1 entry
  1240→        assert_eq!(files_len, 1, "Should detect 1 file with staged changes");
  1241→        assert_eq!(
  1242→            entries_len, 1,
  1243→            "Should track the staged changes in checkpoint"
  1244→        );
  1245→    }
  1246→
  1247→    #[test]
  1248→    fn test_checkpoint_skips_conflicted_files() {
  1249→        // Create a repo with an initial commit
  1250→        let (tmp_repo, mut file, _) = TmpRepo::new_with_base_commit().unwrap();
  1251→
  1252→        // Get the current branch name (whatever the default is)
  1253→        let base_branch = tmp_repo.current_branch().unwrap();
  1254→
  1255→        // Create a branch and make different changes on each branch to create a conflict
  1256→        tmp_repo.create_branch("feature-branch").unwrap();
  1257→
  1258→        // On feature branch, modify the file
  1259→        file.append("Feature branch change\n").unwrap();
  1260→        tmp_repo
  1261→            .trigger_checkpoint_with_author("FeatureUser")
  1262→            .unwrap();
  1263→        tmp_repo.commit_with_message("Feature commit").unwrap();
  1264→
  1265→        // Switch back to base branch and make conflicting changes
  1266→        tmp_repo.switch_branch(&base_branch).unwrap();
  1267→        file.append("Main branch change\n").unwrap();
  1268→        tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("MainUser").unwrap();
  1269→        tmp_repo.commit_with_message("Main commit").unwrap();
  1270→
  1271→        // Attempt to merge feature-branch into base branch - this should create a conflict
  1272→        let has_conflicts = tmp_repo.merge_with_conflicts("feature-branch").unwrap();
  1273→        assert!(has_conflicts, "Should have merge conflicts");
  1274→
  1275→        // Try to checkpoint while there are conflicts
  1276→        let (entries_len, files_len, _) = tmp_repo.trigger_checkpoint_with_author("Human").unwrap();
  1277→
  1278→        // Checkpoint should skip conflicted files
  1279→        assert_eq!(
  1280→            files_len, 0,
  1281→            "Should have 0 files (conflicted file should be skipped)"
  1282→        );
  1283→        assert_eq!(
  1284→            entries_len, 0,
  1285→            "Should have 0 entries (conflicted file should be skipped)"
  1286→        );
  1287→    }

  1289→    #[test]

  1339→    fn test_checkpoint_works_after_conflict_resolution_maintains_authorship() {
  1340→        // Create a repo with an initial commit

  1346→        // Checkpoint initial state to track the base authorship
  1347→        let file_path = file.path();

  1356→        tmp_repo.commit_with_message("Feature commit").unwrap();
  1357→
  1358→        // Switch back to base branch and make conflicting changes
  1359→        tmp_repo.switch_branch(&base_branch).unwrap();
  1360→        file.append("Main line 1\n").unwrap();

  1400→        // After resolution, make additional changes to test that checkpointing works again

  1404→        // Now checkpoint should work and track the new changes

  1515→fn is_text_file(working_log: &PersistedWorkingLog, path: &str) -> bool {
  1516→    // Normalize path for dirty_files lookup
  1517→    let normalized_path = normalize_to_posix(path);
  1518→    let skip_metadata_check = working_log
  1519→        .dirty_files
  1520→        .as_ref()
  1521→        .map(|m| m.contains_key(&normalized_path))
  1522→        .unwrap_or(false);
  1523→
  1524→    if !skip_metadata_check {
  1525→        if let Ok(metadata) = std::fs::metadata(working_log.to_repo_absolute_path(&normalized_path))
  1526→        {
  1527→            if !metadata.is_file() {
  1528→                return false;
  1529→            }
  1530→        } else {
  1531→            return false; // If metadata can't be read, treat as non-text
  1532→        }
  1533→    }
  1534→
  1535→    working_log
  1536→        .read_current_file_content(&normalized_path)
  1537→        .map(|content| !content.chars().any(|c| c == '\0'))
  1538→        .unwrap_or(false)
  1539→}
  1540→
  1541→fn is_text_file_in_head(repo: &Repository, path: &str) -> bool {
  1542→    // For deleted files, check if they were text files in HEAD
  1543→    let head_commit = match repo
  1544→        .head()
  1545→        .ok()
  1546→        .and_then(|h| h.target().ok())
  1547→        .and_then(|oid| repo.find_commit(oid).ok())
  1548→    {
  1549→        Some(commit) => commit,
  1550→        None => return false,
  1551→    };
  1552→
  1553→    let head_tree = match head_commit.tree().ok() {
  1554→        Some(tree) => tree,
  1555→        None => return false,
  1556→    };
  1557→
  1558→    match head_tree.get_path(std::path::Path::new(path)) {
  1559→        Ok(entry) => {
  1560→            if let Ok(blob) = repo.find_blob(entry.id()) {
  1561→                // Consider a file text if it contains no null bytes
  1562→                let blob_content = match blob.content() {
  1563→                    Ok(content) => content,
  1564→                    Err(_) => return false,
  1565→                };
  1566→                !blob_content.contains(&0)
  1567→            } else {
  1568→                false
  1569→            }
  1570→        }
  1571→        Err(_) => false,
  1572→    }
  1573→}
  1574→
  1575→/// Upsert a checkpoint prompt to the internal database
  1576→fn upsert_checkpoint_prompt_to_db(
  1577→    checkpoint: &Checkpoint,
  1578→    workdir: String,
  1579→    commit_sha: Option<String>,
  1580→) -> Result<(), GitAiError> {
  1581→    use crate::authorship::internal_db::{InternalDatabase, PromptDbRecord};
  1582→
  1583→    let record = PromptDbRecord::from_checkpoint(checkpoint, Some(workdir), commit_sha)
  1584→        .ok_or_else(|| {
  1585→            GitAiError::Generic("Failed to create prompt record from checkpoint".to_string())
  1586→        })?;
  1587→
  1588→    let db = InternalDatabase::global()?;
  1589→    let mut db_guard = db
  1590→        .lock()
  1591→        .map_err(|e| GitAiError::Generic(format!("Failed to lock database: {}", e)))?;
  1592→
  1593→    db_guard.upsert_prompt(&record)?;
  1594→
  1595→    Ok(())
  1596→}

    32→    fn check_hooks(&self, _params: &HookInstallerParams) -> Result<HookCheckResult, GitAiError> {

    36→        if !has_binary && !has_dotfiles {

    49→                        return Err(GitAiError::Generic(format!(

    52→                        )));

   133→                "desired_cmd": pre_tool_cmd,
   134→            },
   135→            "PostToolUse": {
   136→                "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit",
   137→                "desired_cmd": post_tool_cmd,
   138→            }
   139→        });
   140→
   141→        // Merge desired into existing
   142→        let mut merged = existing.clone();
   143→        let mut hooks_obj = merged.get("hooks").cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
   144→
   145→        // Process both PreToolUse and PostToolUse
   146→        for hook_type in &["PreToolUse", "PostToolUse"] {
   147→            let desired_matcher = desired_hooks[hook_type]["matcher"].as_str().unwrap();
   148→            let desired_cmd = desired_hooks[hook_type]["desired_cmd"].as_str().unwrap();
   149→
   150→            // Get or create the hooks array for this type
   151→            let mut hook_type_array = hooks_obj
   152→                .get(*hook_type)
   153→                .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
   154→                .cloned()
   155→                .unwrap_or_default();
   156→
   157→            // Find existing matcher block for Write|Edit|MultiEdit
   158→            let mut found_matcher_idx: Option<usize> = None;
   159→            for (idx, item) in hook_type_array.iter().enumerate() {
   160→                if let Some(matcher) = item.get("matcher").and_then(|m| m.as_str()) {
   161→                    if matcher == desired_matcher {
   162→                        found_matcher_idx = Some(idx);
   163→                        break;
   164→                    }
   165→                }
   166→            }
   167→
   168→            let matcher_idx = match found_matcher_idx {
   169→                Some(idx) => idx,
   170→                None => {
   171→                    // Create new matcher block
   172→                    hook_type_array.push(json!({
   173→                        "matcher": desired_matcher,
   174→                        "hooks": []
   175→                    }));
   176→                    hook_type_array.len() - 1
   177→                }
   178→            };
   179→
   180→            // Get the hooks array within this matcher block
   181→            let mut hooks_array = hook_type_array[matcher_idx]
   182→                .get("hooks")
   183→                .and_then(|h| h.as_array())
   184→                .cloned()
   185→                .unwrap_or_default();
   186→
   187→            // Update outdated git-ai checkpoint commands
   188→            let mut found_idx: Option<usize> = None;
   189→            let mut needs_update = false;
   190→
   191→            for (idx, hook) in hooks_array.iter().enumerate() {
   192→                if let Some(cmd) = hook.get("command").and_then(|c| c.as_str()) {
   193→                    if is_git_ai_checkpoint_command(cmd) {
   194→                        if found_idx.is_none() {
   195→                            found_idx = Some(idx);
   196→                            if cmd != desired_cmd {
   197→                                needs_update = true;
   198→                            }
   199→                        }
   200→                    }
   201→                }
   202→            }
   203→
   204→            match found_idx {
   205→                Some(idx) => {
   206→                    if needs_update {
   207→                        hooks_array[idx] = json!({
   208→                            "type": "command",
   209→                            "command": desired_cmd
   210→                        });
   211→                    }
   212→                    // Remove any duplicate git-ai checkpoint commands
   213→                    let keep_idx = idx;
   214→                    let mut current_idx = 0;
   215→                    hooks_array.retain(|hook| {
   216→                        let should_keep = if current_idx == keep_idx {
   217→                            current_idx += 1;
   218→                            true
   219→                        } else if let Some(cmd) = hook.get("command").and_then(|c| c.as_str()) {
   220→                            let is_dup = is_git_ai_checkpoint_command(cmd);
   221→                            current_idx += 1;
   222→                            !is_dup
   223→                        } else {
   224→                            current_idx += 1;
   225→                            true
   226→                        };
   227→                        should_keep
   228→                    });
   229→                }
   230→                None => {
   231→                    // No existing command found, add new one
   232→                    hooks_array.push(json!({
   233→                        "type": "command",
   234→                        "command": desired_cmd
   235→                    }));
   236→                }
   237→            }
   238→
   239→            // Write back the hooks array to the matcher block
   240→            if let Some(matcher_block) = hook_type_array[matcher_idx].as_object_mut() {
   241→                matcher_block.insert("hooks".to_string(), Value::Array(hooks_array));
   242→            }
   243→
   244→            // Write back the updated hook_type_array
   245→            if let Some(obj) = hooks_obj.as_object_mut() {
   246→                obj.insert(hook_type.to_string(), Value::Array(hook_type_array));
   247→            }
   248→        }
   249→
   250→        // Write back hooks to merged
   251→        if let Some(root) = merged.as_object_mut() {
   252→            root.insert("hooks".to_string(), hooks_obj);
   253→        }
   254→
   255→        // Check if there are semantic changes (compare JSON values, not strings)
   256→        if existing == merged {
   257→            return Ok(None);
   258→        }
   259→
   260→        // Generate new content
   261→        let new_content = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&merged)?;
   262→
   263→        // Generate diff
   264→        let diff_output = generate_diff(&settings_path, &existing_content, &new_content);
   265→
   266→        // Write if not dry-run
   267→        if !dry_run {
   268→            write_atomic(&settings_path, new_content.as_bytes())?;
   269→        }
   270→
   271→        Ok(Some(diff_output))
   272→    }
   273→
   274→    fn uninstall_hooks(
   275→        &self,
   276→        _params: &HookInstallerParams,
   277→        dry_run: bool,
   278→    ) -> Result<Option<String>, GitAiError> {
   279→        let settings_path = Self::settings_path();
   280→
   281→        if !settings_path.exists() {
   282→            return Ok(None);
   283→        }
   284→
   285→        let existing_content = fs::read_to_string(&settings_path)?;
   286→        let existing: Value = serde_json::from_str(&existing_content)?;
   287→
   288→        let mut merged = existing.clone();
   289→        let mut hooks_obj = match merged.get("hooks").cloned() {
   290→            Some(h) => h,
   291→            None => return Ok(None),
   292→        };
   293→
   294→        let mut changed = false;
   295→
   296→        // Remove git-ai checkpoint commands from both PreToolUse and PostToolUse
   297→        for hook_type in &["PreToolUse", "PostToolUse"] {
   298→            if let Some(hook_type_array) = hooks_obj.get_mut(*hook_type).and_then(|v| v.as_array_mut()) {
   299→                for matcher_block in hook_type_array.iter_mut() {
   300→                    if let Some(hooks_array) = matcher_block.get_mut("hooks").and_then(|h| h.as_array_mut()) {
   301→                        let original_len = hooks_array.len();
   302→                        hooks_array.retain(|hook| {
   303→                            if let Some(cmd) = hook.get("command").and_then(|c| c.as_str()) {
   304→                                !is_git_ai_checkpoint_command(cmd)
   305→                            } else {
   306→                                true
   307→                            }
   308→                        });
   309→                        if hooks_array.len() != original_len {
   310→                            changed = true;
   311→                        }
   312→                    }
   313→                }
   314→            }
   315→        }
   316→
   317→        if !changed {
   318→            return Ok(None);
   319→        }
   320→
   321→        // Write back hooks to merged
   322→        if let Some(root) = merged.as_object_mut() {
   323→            root.insert("hooks".to_string(), hooks_obj);
   324→        }
   325→
   326→        let new_content = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&merged)?;
   327→        let diff_output = generate_diff(&settings_path, &existing_content, &new_content);
   328→
   329→        if !dry_run {
   330→            write_atomic(&settings_path, new_content.as_bytes())?;
   331→        }
   332→
   333→        Ok(Some(diff_output))
   334→    }
   335→}

> AGENT

Found it. Their "standard" is the **`checkpoint agent-v1` CLI command** with a specific JSON schema via stdin.

## git-ai Agent Integration Standard

### The Interface

Agents call:
```bash
echo '<json>' | git-ai checkpoint agent-v1 --hook-input stdin
```

### JSON Schema (agent-v1)

**For human checkpoints** (before AI edits):
```json
{
  "type": "human",
  "repo_working_dir": "/path/to/repo",
  "will_edit_filepaths": ["src/file.ts"]
}
```

**For AI checkpoints** (after AI edits):
```json
{
  "type": "ai_agent",
  "repo_working_dir": "/path/to/repo",
  "agent_name": "claude-code",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  "conversation_id": "session-uuid",
  "edited_filepaths": ["src/file.ts"],
  "transcript": {
    "messages": [
      {"type": "user", "text": "..."},
      {"type": "assistant", "text": "..."},
      {"type": "tool_use", "name": "Edit", "input": {...}}
    ]
  }
}
```

### Integration Pattern

For Claude Code specifically, they modify `~/.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "git-ai checkpoint claude --hook-input stdin"
      }]
    }],
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Write|Edit|MultiEdit", 
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "git-ai checkpoint claude --hook-input stdin"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

The flow:
1. **PreToolUse hook** → Create "human" checkpoint (marks prior changes as human)
2. Agent makes file edits
3. **PostToolUse hook** → Create "ai_agent" checkpoint with transcript

### Key Data Captured

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `agent_name` | Tool identifier (e.g., "claude-code", "cursor") |
| `model` | Model used (e.g., "claude-sonnet-4-20250514") |
| `conversation_id` | Session/thread identifier for hash generation |
| `edited_filepaths` | Files touched in this edit |
| `transcript.messages` | Full conversation (minus tool responses) |

The session hash is derived from: `SHA256("{agent_name}:{conversation_id}")[:16]`

### Comparison to Entire CLI

**git-ai approach:**
- External CLI command called via hooks
- JSON over stdin
- Line-level attribution computed post-hoc
- Requires agents to call the CLI at right moments

**Entire CLI approach:**
- Agent-specific adapters read native session files (JSONL for Claude)
- Session state tracked in `.git/entire-sessions/`
- Commit-level attribution via trailers
- More passive - reads existing session data rather than requiring callbacks

> AGENT

Based on my analysis, here's the summary:

## Entire CLI Line-Level Attribution

### What We Actually Track

| Data | Auto-Commit | Manual-Commit |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| **Files touched** | ✅ `FilesTouched` list | ✅ `FilesTouched` list |
| **Full tree state** | ✅ Git commit captures it | ✅ Shadow branch captures it |
| **Line-level ranges** | ❌ Not tracked | ❌ Not tracked |

### Auto-Commit Strategy

**What we have:**
- The commit diff IS the agent's work (git's native line tracking)
- `git blame` on that commit shows the agent session
- Trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123` links to full transcript

**Gap:**
- If user edits files before our commit hook fires, we don't distinguish "agent wrote lines 1-10, human edited line 5"
- The whole commit is attributed to the session

### Manual-Commit Strategy  

**What we have:**
- Shadow branch captures exact tree state at each checkpoint
- Can diff between checkpoints to see what changed
- On rewind, restore exact file contents from that checkpoint

**Gap:**
- User can modify files between checkpoint and their manual commit
- We don't track "agent wrote lines 1-10, then human added lines 11-15 before committing"
- The final commit may include human changes not in any checkpoint

### Comparison to git-ai

| Feature | git-ai | Entire CLI |
|---------|--------|------------|
| **Attribution level** | Line ranges per file | Commit/checkpoint level |
| **Human interleaving** | Tracks human vs AI per line | All-or-nothing per checkpoint |
| **Storage format** | Attestation section with line ranges | File list + tree snapshot |
| **Query capability** | "Who wrote line 42?" | "Which session made this commit?" |

### Example Scenario

User asks Claude to add a function, then manually fixes a typo before committing:

**git-ai captures:**
```
src/auth.rs
  abc123 1-20,25-30    # AI wrote these lines
  human  21-24         # Human edited these lines
```

**Entire CLI captures:**
```
Checkpoint 1: tree has auth.rs with lines 1-30
Commit: Entire-Checkpoint: xyz789 → links to session transcript
# No visibility into which lines were human vs AI
```

### Potential Enhancement

To match git-ai's granularity, we'd need to:
1. Track file content hash at each checkpoint
2. On commit, diff checkpoint tree vs actual commit tree
3. Attribute the delta to "human edits between checkpoint and commit"

But this adds significant complexity for a feature that may not be critical if the goal is session-level attribution rather than line-level blame.

> DEVELOPER

3. Attribute the delta to "human edits between checkpoint and commit"

Also that attribution is fragile since a rebase can just change those lines slightly, right?

> AGENT

Exactly. Even git-ai's line-level attribution is fragile in practice:

**The attribution chain breaks when:**

| Operation | git-ai (with hooks) | git-ai (without hooks) | Entire CLI |
|-----------|---------------------|------------------------|------------|
| Local rebase | ✅ Recalculates lines | ❌ Notes orphaned | N/A (commit-level) |
| GitHub squash merge | ❌ Notes orphaned | ❌ Notes orphaned | ✅ Trailer preserved |
| GitHub rebase merge | ❌ Notes orphaned | ❌ Notes orphaned | ✅ Trailer preserved |
| Cherry-pick (no hooks) | ❌ Notes orphaned | ❌ Notes orphaned | ✅ Trailer preserved |

**The fundamental issue:**

Line-level attribution requires constant recalculation as code moves around. Every time content shifts:
- Line numbers change
- git-ai must intercept and recalculate
- If that recalculation doesn't happen → data is wrong or orphaned

**Commit-level attribution is more durable:**

The trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: abc123` is just text in the commit message. It survives:
- Rebases (message content preserved)
- Squash merges (trailers aggregated)
- Cherry-picks (message comes along)

The metadata on `entire/sessions` branch is keyed by that checkpoint ID, not by commit SHA. So even if the commit SHA changes 10 times through rebases, the link remains valid.

**The trade-off:**

| Approach | Granularity | Durability |
|----------|-------------|------------|
| git-ai line-level | High (per-line) | Fragile (requires hooks everywhere) |
| Entire commit-level | Lower (per-commit) | Robust (survives git operations) |

For most use cases ("which AI session produced this feature?"), commit-level attribution is sufficient and doesn't require the complex machinery of intercepting every git operation and recalculating line ranges.

> DEVELOPER

can we split commits in a commit hook?

> AGENT

Interesting idea. You're thinking: detect human edits beyond the checkpoint and split them into separate commits automatically?

**Git hooks can't directly split commits, but there's a workaround:**

```
pre-commit hook:
1. Compare staged files to last checkpoint tree
2. If "extra" changes detected:
   - Stash the delta (human changes)
   - Let commit proceed with checkpoint-only changes
   - Post-commit: notify user "you have uncommitted human edits"
```

**The flow would be:**

```
User stages everything:     A + B + C (A,B from agent, C from human)
                               ↓
pre-commit detects C is beyond checkpoint
                               ↓
Stash C, commit A + B with agent attribution
                               ↓
post-commit: "Human changes stashed, run `git stash pop && git commit` to commit them"
                               ↓
User commits C separately with no agent attribution
```

**Challenges:**

| Issue | Problem |
|-------|---------|
| **Partial file changes** | If human edited lines 5-10 of a file the agent created, you can't stash "just those lines" |
| **Interleaved edits** | Human might have edited in the middle of agent code |
| **User confusion** | "Why did my commit only include half my changes?" |
| **Merge conflicts** | Stash pop might conflict with what was just committed |

**The partial file problem is the killer:**

git-ai can track line-level because they checkpoint *before and after each tool call*. So they know the exact state before/after each AI edit.

We checkpoint at session-level, so if the user edits a file the agent also touched, we'd need to diff at line-level to separate them - which brings us back to the same fragile line-tracking problem.

**A simpler approach might be:**

Just warn the user in `prepare-commit-msg`:

```
⚠️  Files modified beyond last checkpoint:
   - src/auth.rs (12 lines differ from checkpoint)
   
These changes will be attributed to this session.
To commit agent and human changes separately, abort and commit in stages.
```

That's a clever middle ground. Calculate the attribution percentage at commit time as a one-shot metric.

**The approach:**

```
prepare-commit-msg hook (manual-commit):
1. Get latest checkpoint tree from shadow branch
2. Diff checkpoint tree vs staged changes
3. Calculate: lines matching vs lines different
4. Add metric to commit trailer or metadata
```

**Output could be:**

```
Entire-Checkpoint: abc123
Entire-Agent-Lines: 142
Entire-Human-Lines: 18
Entire-Attribution: 89%
```

Or just store in `metadata.json` on `entire/sessions`:

```json
{
  "checkpoint_id": "abc123",
  "attribution": {
    "agent_lines": 142,
    "human_lines": 18,
    "agent_percentage": 89
  }
}
```

**Why this works:**

| Concern | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Rebase changes line numbers | Doesn't matter - percentage calculated once at commit time |
| Stored where? | In metadata, not tied to specific lines |
| Survives squash merge | Yes - it's just metadata in `entire/sessions` |
| Complexity | Low - just a diff at commit time |

**Calculation options:**

```go
// Simple: total lines
agentPct = checkpointLines / committedLines

// Better: account for modifications
added := lines in commit but not in checkpoint
removed := lines in checkpoint but not in commit  
modified := lines that changed
unchanged := lines that match exactly

agentPct = unchanged / (unchanged + added + modified)
```

**Use cases:**

- Analytics dashboard: "Average AI contribution across commits: 73%"
- Session quality signal: heavily-edited sessions might indicate poor suggestions
- Audit trail: "This feature was 95% AI-generated"

This gives you useful attribution data without the fragile line-tracking machinery. The number is meaningful and durable.

|----------|--------------|
| File not in checkpoint but in commit | `"human_added_file"` |

| File 100% unchanged | `"exact_match"` |

## Summary: Manual-Commit Strategy Hooks & Condensation Implementation

I've explored the manual-commit strategy hooks and condensation logic. Here's a comprehensive overview:

---

### 1. **How the Post-Commit Hook Works**

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` (lines 345-494)

The `PostCommit()` function is the entry point:

1. **Check for Checkpoint Trailer** (lines 360-379):
   - Reads HEAD commit message
   - Looks for `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
   - If missing, treats as manual commit → silent exit

2. **Find Active Sessions** (lines 381-420):
   - Finds sessions matching this worktree
   - Filters to sessions with new content (transcripts with more lines than `CondensedTranscriptLines`)
   - If none found, updates `BaseCommit` to HEAD (to prevent stale base commits)

3. **Condense Each Session** (lines 425-473):
   - For each session with new content, calls `CondenseSession()`
   - Tracks shadow branches for cleanup
   - Updates session state after condensation:
     - `BaseCommit` → new HEAD
     - `CheckpointCount` → 0 (reset for new shadow branch)
     - `CondensedTranscriptLines` → new total
     - `LastCheckpointID` → checkpoint ID (for reuse on future commits)

4. **Cleanup Shadow Branches** (lines 475-491):
   - Deletes old shadow branches (data is now on `entire/sessions`)
   - Prints feedback to user

---

### 2. **Condensation Logic: Shadow to entire/sessions**

**Main File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go` (lines 96-158)

**Key Function:** `CondenseSession()`

**Process:**
1. Gets shadow branch for base commit
2. Calls `extractSessionData()` to pull metadata from shadow branch tree
3. Gets `GitStore` (checkpoint abstraction)
4. Calls `store.WriteCommitted()` with:
   - Checkpoint ID (from `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer)
   - Session ID
   - Extracted transcript, prompts, context
   - Files touched from `SessionState`
   - Strategy name, branch name, author info
   - Token usage data

**Returns:** `CondenseResult` with checkpoint ID, session ID, count of checkpoints, and total transcript lines.

---

### 3. **How metadata.json is Currently Written**

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go` (lines 320-380)

**Function:** `writeMetadataJSON()`

**Current Structure:**
```go
type CommittedMetadata struct {
    CheckpointID           id.CheckpointID
    SessionID              string
    Strategy               string
    CreatedAt              time.Time
    Branch                 string
    CheckpointsCount       int           // # of checkpoints on shadow
    FilesTouched           []string
    Agent                  agent.AgentType
    IsTask                 bool
    ToolUseID              string
    SessionCount           int            // # of sessions (1 if omitted)
    SessionIDs             []string       // All session IDs in checkpoint
    TranscriptUUIDAtStart  string         // Optional
    TranscriptLinesAtStart int            // Optional
    TokenUsage             *agent.TokenUsage
}
```

**Key Features:**
- **Single-session checkpoint:** SessionCount = 1, SessionIDs = [current session]
- **Multi-session checkpoint (archiving):** SessionCount > 1, SessionIDs = [previous sessions + current]
- **Merging on collision:** 
  - If checkpoint already exists (same ID), archives old session to numbered subfolder (`1/`, `2/`, etc.)
  - Merges `FilesTouched` lists (deduplicates)
  - Increments `SessionCount`
  - Appends session IDs

---

This is the critical architectural point:

#### **Access in `CondenseSession()`** (lines 100-158):

### 5. **Tree Construction Timeline**

```
Post-Commit Hook Triggered
    ↓
PostCommit() reads HEAD commit message
    ↓
Extract checkpointID from Entire-Checkpoint trailer
    ↓
CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
    ├─ getSessionsBranchRef() → Get COMMITTED tree (entire/sessions)
    │   └─ FlattenTree() → Build flattened entry map of current entire/sessions
    │
    ├─ extractSessionData(repo, shadowRef, ...) → Read from SHADOW branch tree
    │   └─ tree.File(metadataDir + "/full.jsonl") → Get transcript
    │
    └─ store.WriteCommitted(opts)
        ├─ buildCommitMessage() → "Checkpoint: <id>"
        ├─ writeStandardCheckpointEntries(opts, basePath, entries)
        │   ├─ Check for existing checkpoint (archiving)
        │   ├─ Write transcript (from opts extracted above)
        │   ├─ Write prompts, context
        │   └─ writeMetadataJSON() ← WRITES metadata.json HERE
        │
        ├─ BuildTreeFromEntries() → Build new tree with updated entries
        ├─ createCommit(newTreeHash, ref.Hash(), ...) → Create commit on entire/sessions
        └─ SetReference() → Move entire/sessions ref to new commit
```

### 7. **Critical Insights for Your Work**

1. **Both trees available:** `WriteCommitted()` receives extracted checkpoint data in `opts` and reads the current committed tree to flatten it into `entries` map.

2. **Tree merging happens here:** When writing to `entire/sessions`:
   - Start with current tree (flattened to entries map)
   - Add/overwrite entries for new checkpoint at sharded path
   - Handle archiving if checkpoint ID collides

3. **metadata.json written at:** Line 266 in `checkpoint/committed.go` calls `writeMetadataJSON()` which:
   - Constructs metadata struct with all fields
   - Handles multi-session merging if checkpoint exists
   - Marshals to JSON blob

   - Blob is included when tree is rebuilt

4. **Session state updates after commit:** In `manual_commit_hooks.go` lines 437-456, session state is updated with:
   - New `BaseCommit` (HEAD hash)
   - Reset `CheckpointCount` to 0
   - Updated `CondensedTranscriptLines`
