   136→// SaveTaskCheckpoint saves a task checkpoint to the shadow branch.
   137→// Uses checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporaryTask for git operations.
   138→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx TaskCheckpointContext) error {
   139→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   140→	if err != nil {
   141→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   142→	}
   143→
   144→	// Load session state
   145→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx.SessionID)
   146→	if err != nil || state == nil || state.BaseCommit == "" {
   147→		// Initialize if needed (including if BaseCommit is empty from partial warning state)
   148→		// Preserve existing AgentType if we have a partial state, otherwise use default
   149→		agentType := DefaultAgentType
   150→		if state != nil && state.AgentType != "" {
   151→			agentType = state.AgentType
   152→		}
   153→		state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, ctx.SessionID, agentType, "") // No transcript path in fallback
   154→		if err != nil {
   155→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session for task checkpoint: %w", err)
   156→		}
   157→	}
   158→
   159→	// Get checkpoint store
   160→	store, err := s.getCheckpointStore()
   161→	if err != nil {
   162→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get checkpoint store: %w", err)
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Check if shadow branch exists to report whether we created it
   166→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)
   167→	branchExisted := store.ShadowBranchExists(state.BaseCommit)
   168→
   169→	// Compute metadata paths for commit message
   170→	sessionMetadataDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromEntireID(ctx.SessionID)
   171→	taskMetadataDir := TaskMetadataDir(sessionMetadataDir, ctx.ToolUseID)
   172→
   173→	// Generate commit message
   174→	shortToolUseID := ctx.ToolUseID
   175→	if len(shortToolUseID) > 12 {
   176→		shortToolUseID = shortToolUseID[:12]
   177→	}
   178→
   179→	var messageSubject string
   180→	if ctx.IsIncremental {
   181→		messageSubject = FormatIncrementalSubject(
   182→			ctx.IncrementalType,
   183→			ctx.SubagentType,
   184→			ctx.TaskDescription,
   185→			ctx.TodoContent,
   186→			ctx.IncrementalSequence,
   187→			shortToolUseID,
   188→		)
   189→	} else {
   190→		messageSubject = FormatSubagentEndMessage(ctx.SubagentType, ctx.TaskDescription, shortToolUseID)
   191→	}
   192→	commitMsg := trailers.FormatShadowTaskCommit(
   193→		messageSubject,
   194→		taskMetadataDir,
   195→		ctx.SessionID,
   196→	)
   197→
   198→	// Use WriteTemporaryTask to create the checkpoint
   199→	_, err = store.WriteTemporaryTask(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryTaskOptions{
   200→		SessionID:              ctx.SessionID,
   201→		BaseCommit:             state.BaseCommit,
   202→		ToolUseID:              ctx.ToolUseID,
   203→		AgentID:                ctx.AgentID,
   204→		ModifiedFiles:          ctx.ModifiedFiles,
   205→		NewFiles:               ctx.NewFiles,
   206→		DeletedFiles:           ctx.DeletedFiles,
   207→		TranscriptPath:         ctx.TranscriptPath,
   208→		SubagentTranscriptPath: ctx.SubagentTranscriptPath,
   209→		CheckpointUUID:         ctx.CheckpointUUID,
   210→		CommitMessage:          commitMsg,
   211→		AuthorName:             ctx.AuthorName,
   212→		AuthorEmail:            ctx.AuthorEmail,
   213→		IsIncremental:          ctx.IsIncremental,
   214→		IncrementalSequence:    ctx.IncrementalSequence,
   215→		IncrementalType:        ctx.IncrementalType,
   216→		IncrementalData:        ctx.IncrementalData,
   217→	})
   218→	if err != nil {
   219→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write task checkpoint: %w", err)
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Track touched files (modified, new, and deleted)
   223→	state.FilesTouched = mergeFilesTouched(state.FilesTouched, ctx.ModifiedFiles, ctx.NewFiles, ctx.DeletedFiles)
   224→
   225→	// Save updated state
   226→	if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   227→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	if !branchExisted {
   231→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Created shadow branch '%s' and committed task checkpoint\n", shadowBranchName)
   232→	} else {
   233→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Committed task checkpoint to shadow branch '%s'\n", shadowBranchName)
   234→	}
   235→
   236→	// Log task checkpoint creation
   237→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   238→	attrs := []any{
   239→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   240→		slog.String("checkpoint_type", "task"),
   241→		slog.String("checkpoint_uuid", ctx.CheckpointUUID),
   242→		slog.String("tool_use_id", ctx.ToolUseID),
   243→		slog.String("subagent_type", ctx.SubagentType),
   244→		slog.Int("modified_files", len(ctx.ModifiedFiles)),
   245→		slog.Int("new_files", len(ctx.NewFiles)),
   246→		slog.Int("deleted_files", len(ctx.DeletedFiles)),
   247→		slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   248→		slog.Bool("branch_created", !branchExisted),
   249→	}
   250→	if ctx.IsIncremental {
   251→		attrs = append(attrs,
   252→			slog.Bool("is_incremental", true),
   253→			slog.String("incremental_type", ctx.IncrementalType),
   254→			slog.Int("incremental_sequence", ctx.IncrementalSequence),
   255→		)
   256→	}
   257→	logging.Info(logCtx, "task checkpoint saved", attrs...)
   258→
   259→	return nil
   260→}

   262→// mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
   263→func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
   264→	seen := make(map[string]bool)
   265→	for _, f := range existing {
   266→		seen[f] = true
   267→	}
   268→
   269→	for _, list := range fileLists {
   270→		for _, f := range list {
   271→			seen[f] = true
   272→		}
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
   276→	for f := range seen {
   277→		result = append(result, f)
   278→	}
   279→
   280→	// Sort for deterministic output
   281→	sort.Strings(result)
   282→	return result
   283→}
   284→
   285→// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   286→// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   287→func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   288→	if incoming == nil {
   289→		return existing
   290→	}
   291→	if existing == nil {
   292→		// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   293→		return &agent.TokenUsage{
   294→			InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   295→			CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   296→			CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   297→			OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   298→			APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   299→			SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   300→		}
   301→	}
   302→
   303→	// Accumulate values
   304→	existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   305→	existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   306→	existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   307→	existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   308→	existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   309→
   310→	// Accumulate subagent tokens if present
   311→	if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   312→		existing.SubagentTokens = accumulateTokenUsage(existing.SubagentTokens, incoming.SubagentTokens)
   313→	}
   314→
   315→	return existing
   316→}
   317→
   318→// deleteShadowBranch deletes a shadow branch by name using an existing repo handle.
   319→// Returns nil if the branch doesn't exist (idempotent).
   320→func deleteShadowBranch(repo *git.Repository, branchName string) error {
   321→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   322→
   323→	// Check if reference exists
   324→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   325→	if err != nil {
   326→		// Branch doesn't exist - nothing to delete (idempotent)
   327→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Not an error condition - branch already gone
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	// Delete the reference
   331→	if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(ref.Name()); err != nil {
   332→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete branch %s: %w", branchName, err)
   333→	}
   334→
   335→	return nil
   336→}

    24→// State represents the state of an active session.

    42→	// CondensedTranscriptLines tracks lines already included in previous condensation
    43→	CondensedTranscriptLines int `json:"condensed_transcript_lines,omitempty"`
    44→
    45→	// UntrackedFilesAtStart tracks files that existed at session start (to preserve during rewind)
    46→	UntrackedFilesAtStart []string `json:"untracked_files_at_start,omitempty"`
    47→

    53→

    71→// StateStore provides low-level operations for managing session state files.
    72→//
    73→// StateStore is a primitive for session state persistence. It is NOT the same as
    74→// the Sessions interface - it only handles state files in .git/entire-sessions/,
    75→// not the full session data which includes checkpoint content.
    76→//
    77→// Use StateStore directly in strategies for performance-critical state operations.
    78→// Use the Sessions interface (when implemented) for high-level session management.
    79→type StateStore struct {
    80→	// stateDir is the directory where session state files are stored
    81→	stateDir string
    82→}
    83→
    84→// NewStateStore creates a new state store.
    85→// Uses the git common dir to store session state (shared across worktrees).
    86→func NewStateStore() (*StateStore, error) {
    87→	commonDir, err := getGitCommonDir()
    88→	if err != nil {
    89→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
    90→	}
    91→	return &StateStore{
    92→		stateDir: filepath.Join(commonDir, sessionStateDirName),
    93→	}, nil
    94→}
    95→
    96→// NewStateStoreWithDir creates a new state store with a custom directory.
    97→// This is useful for testing.
    98→func NewStateStoreWithDir(stateDir string) *StateStore {
    99→	return &StateStore{stateDir: stateDir}
   100→}
   101→
   102→// Load loads the session state for the given session ID.
   103→// Returns (nil, nil) when session file doesn't exist (not an error condition).
   104→func (s *StateStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) (*State, error) {
   105→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   106→
   107→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   108→	if err := paths.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   109→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   110→	}
   111→
   112→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   113→
   114→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile) //nolint:gosec // stateFile is derived from sessionID
   115→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   116→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil,nil indicates session not found (expected case)
   117→	}
   118→	if err != nil {
   119→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   120→	}
   121→
   122→	var state State
   123→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   124→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal session state: %w", err)
   125→	}
   126→	return &state, nil
   127→}
   128→
   129→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   130→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   131→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   132→
   133→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   134→	if err := paths.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   135→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   136→	}
   137→
   138→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   139→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   140→	}
   141→
   142→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   143→	if err != nil {
   144→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   145→	}
   146→
   147→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   148→
   149→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   150→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   151→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   152→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   153→	}
   154→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   155→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   156→	}
   157→	return nil
   158→}
   159→
   160→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   161→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   162→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   163→
   164→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   165→	if err := paths.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   166→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   167→	}
   168→
   169→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   170→
   171→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   172→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   173→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   174→		}
   175→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   176→	}
   177→	return nil
   178→}
   179→
   180→// List returns all session states.
   181→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   182→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   183→
   184→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   185→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   186→		return nil, nil
   187→	}
   188→	if err != nil {
   189→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   190→	}
   191→
   192→	var states []*State
   193→	for _, entry := range entries {
   194→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   195→			continue
   196→		}
   197→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   198→			continue // Skip temp files
   199→		}
   200→
   201→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   202→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   203→		if err != nil {
   204→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   205→		}
   206→		if state == nil {
   207→			continue
   208→		}
   209→
   210→		states = append(states, state)
   211→	}
   212→	return states, nil
   213→}
   214→
   215→// FindByBaseCommit finds all sessions based on the given commit hash.
   216→func (s *StateStore) FindByBaseCommit(ctx context.Context, baseCommit string) ([]*State, error) {
   217→	allStates, err := s.List(ctx)
   218→	if err != nil {
   219→		return nil, err
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	var matching []*State
   223→	for _, state := range allStates {
   224→		if state.BaseCommit == baseCommit {
   225→			matching = append(matching, state)
   226→		}
   227→	}
   228→	return matching, nil
   229→}
   230→
   231→// FindByWorktree finds all sessions for the given worktree path.
   232→func (s *StateStore) FindByWorktree(ctx context.Context, worktreePath string) ([]*State, error) {
   233→	allStates, err := s.List(ctx)
   234→	if err != nil {
   235→		return nil, err
   236→	}
   237→
   238→	var matching []*State
   239→	for _, state := range allStates {
   240→		if state.WorktreePath == worktreePath {
   241→			matching = append(matching, state)
   242→		}
   243→	}
   244→	return matching, nil
   245→}
   246→
   247→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   248→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   249→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   250→}
   251→
   252→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   253→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   254→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   255→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   256→	ctx := context.Background()
   257→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   258→	cmd.Dir = "."
   259→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   260→	if err != nil {
   261→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   262→	}
   263→
   264→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   265→
   266→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   267→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   268→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   269→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   270→	}
   271→
   272→	return filepath.Clean(commonDir), nil
   273→}
   274→
   275→// GetWorktreePath returns the absolute path to the current worktree root.
   276→func GetWorktreePath() (string, error) {
   277→	ctx := context.Background()
   278→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
   279→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   280→	if err != nil {
   281→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree path: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
   284→}

    11→
    12→// CalculateAttribution computes line-level attribution for the commit by comparing:
    13→// - baseTree: state before the session (parent commit)
    14→// - checkpointTree: what the agent wrote (shadow branch)
    15→// - committedTree: what was actually committed (HEAD)
    16→//
    17→// This measures how much of the commit's diff came from the agent vs human edits.
    18→// Only counts lines that actually changed in the commit, not total file sizes.
    19→//
    20→// Returns nil if filesTouched is empty.
    21→func CalculateAttribution(
    22→	baseTree *object.Tree,
    23→	checkpointTree *object.Tree,
    24→	committedTree *object.Tree,
    25→	filesTouched []string,
    26→) *checkpoint.InitialAttribution {
    27→	if len(filesTouched) == 0 {
    28→		return nil
    29→	}
    30→
    31→	var totalAgentAdded, totalHumanAdded, totalHumanModified, totalHumanRemoved, totalCommitAdded int
    32→
    33→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
    34→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
    35→		checkpointContent := getFileContent(checkpointTree, filePath)
    36→		committedContent := getFileContent(committedTree, filePath)
    37→
    38→		// Skip if nothing changed in the commit for this file
    39→		if baseContent == committedContent {
    40→			continue
    41→		}
    42→
    43→		// Lines added in this commit (base → committed)
    44→		_, commitAdded, commitRemoved := diffLines(baseContent, committedContent)
    45→
    46→		// Lines human changed from agent's work (checkpoint → committed)
    47→		_, humanAdded, humanRemoved := diffLines(checkpointContent, committedContent)
    48→
    49→		// Agent's contribution = lines added in commit that came from checkpoint (not human)
    50→		// If checkpoint == committed, all commit additions came from agent
    51→		// If human added lines, subtract those from the total
    52→		agentAdded := commitAdded - humanAdded
    53→		if agentAdded < 0 {
    54→			agentAdded = 0
    55→		}
    56→
    57→		// Estimate modified lines (human changed existing agent lines)
    58→		humanModified := min(humanAdded, humanRemoved)
    59→		pureHumanAdded := humanAdded - humanModified
    60→		pureHumanRemoved := humanRemoved - humanModified
    61→
    62→		// For removed lines in commit: if agent removed them (not in checkpoint), don't count as human
    63→		// Only count as human removed if agent kept them but human removed
    64→		agentRemovedFromBase := countLinesStr(baseContent) - countLinesStr(checkpointContent)
    65→		if agentRemovedFromBase < 0 {
    66→			agentRemovedFromBase = 0
    67→		}
    68→		actualHumanRemoved := commitRemoved - agentRemovedFromBase
    69→		if actualHumanRemoved < 0 {
    70→			actualHumanRemoved = 0
    71→		}
    72→		// But cap it at what we detected from checkpoint→committed diff
    73→		if actualHumanRemoved > pureHumanRemoved {
    74→			actualHumanRemoved = pureHumanRemoved
    75→		}
    76→
    77→		totalAgentAdded += agentAdded
    78→		totalHumanAdded += pureHumanAdded
    79→		totalHumanModified += humanModified
    80→		totalHumanRemoved += actualHumanRemoved
    81→		totalCommitAdded += commitAdded
    82→	}
    83→
    84→	// Total lines in commit = lines added (what we're attributing)
    85→	totalInCommit := totalCommitAdded
    86→	if totalInCommit == 0 {
    87→		// If only deletions, use agent lines as the metric
    88→		totalInCommit = totalAgentAdded
    89→	}
    90→
    91→	// Calculate percentage (avoid division by zero)
    92→	var agentPercentage float64
    93→	if totalInCommit > 0 {
    94→		agentPercentage = float64(totalAgentAdded) / float64(totalInCommit) * 100
    95→	}
    96→
    97→	return &checkpoint.InitialAttribution{
    98→		CalculatedAt:    time.Now(),
    99→		AgentLines:      totalAgentAdded,
   100→		HumanAdded:      totalHumanAdded,
   101→		HumanModified:   totalHumanModified,
   102→		HumanRemoved:    totalHumanRemoved,
   103→		TotalCommitted:  totalInCommit,
   104→		AgentPercentage: agentPercentage,
   105→	}
   106→}
   107→
   108→// getFileContent retrieves the content of a file from a tree.
   109→// Returns empty string if the file doesn't exist or can't be read.
   110→func getFileContent(tree *object.Tree, path string) string {
   111→	if tree == nil {
   112→		return ""
   113→	}
   114→
   115→	file, err := tree.File(path)
   116→	if err != nil {
   117→		return ""
   118→	}
   119→
   120→	content, err := file.Contents()
   121→	if err != nil {
   122→		return ""
   123→	}
   124→
   125→	// Skip binary files (contain null bytes)
   126→	if strings.Contains(content, "\x00") {
   127→		return ""
   128→	}
   129→
   130→	return content
   131→}
   132→
   133→// diffLines compares two strings and returns line-level diff stats.
   134→// Returns (unchanged, added, removed) line counts.
   135→func diffLines(checkpointContent, committedContent string) (unchanged, added, removed int) {
   136→	// Handle edge cases
   137→	if checkpointContent == committedContent {
   138→		return countLinesStr(committedContent), 0, 0
   139→	}
   140→	if checkpointContent == "" {
   141→		return 0, countLinesStr(committedContent), 0
   142→	}
   143→	if committedContent == "" {
   144→		return 0, 0, countLinesStr(checkpointContent)
   145→	}
   146→
   147→	dmp := diffmatchpatch.New()
   148→
   149→	// Convert to line-based diff using DiffLinesToChars/DiffCharsToLines pattern
   150→	text1, text2, lineArray := dmp.DiffLinesToChars(checkpointContent, committedContent)
   151→	diffs := dmp.DiffMain(text1, text2, false)
   152→	diffs = dmp.DiffCharsToLines(diffs, lineArray)
   153→
   154→	for _, d := range diffs {
   155→		lines := countLinesInText(d.Text)
   156→		switch d.Type {
   157→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffEqual:
   158→			unchanged += lines
   159→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffInsert:
   160→			added += lines
   161→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffDelete:
   162→			removed += lines
   163→		}
   164→	}
   165→
   166→	return unchanged, added, removed
   167→}
   168→
   169→// countLinesStr returns the number of lines in content string.
   170→// An empty string has 0 lines. A string without newlines has 1 line.
   171→func countLinesStr(content string) int {
   172→	if content == "" {
   173→		return 0
   174→	}
   175→	lines := strings.Count(content, "\n")
   176→	// If content doesn't end with newline, add 1 for the last line
   177→	if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
   178→		lines++
   179→	}
   180→	return lines
   181→}
   182→
   183→// countLinesInText counts lines in a diff text segment.
   184→// Similar to countLines but handles the diff output format.
   185→func countLinesInText(text string) int {
   186→	if text == "" {
   187→		return 0
   188→	}
   189→	// Count newlines as line separators
   190→	lines := strings.Count(text, "\n")
   191→	// If text doesn't end with newline and is not empty, count the last line
   192→	if !strings.HasSuffix(text, "\n") && len(text) > 0 {
   193→		lines++
   194→	}
   195→	return lines
   196→}
   197→

  "new_string": "// countLinesInText counts lines in a diff text segment.\n// Similar to countLines but handles the diff output format.\nfunc countLinesInText(text string) int {\n\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\t// Count newlines as line separators\n\tlines := strings.Count(text, \"\\n\")\n\t// If text doesn't end with newline and is not empty, count the last line\n\tif !strings.HasSuffix(text, \"\\n\") && len(text) > 0 {\n\t\tlines++\n\t}\n\treturn lines\n}\n\n// CalculatePromptAttribution computes line-level attribution at the start of a prompt.\n// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent makes changes.\n//\n// Parameters:\n//   - baseTree: the tree at session start (the base commit)\n//   - lastCheckpointTree: the tree from the previous checkpoint (nil if first checkpoint)\n//   - worktreeFiles: map of file path → current worktree content for files that changed\n//   - checkpointNumber: which checkpoint we're about to create (1-indexed)\n//\n// Returns the attribution data to store in session state.\nfunc CalculatePromptAttribution(\n\tbaseTree *object.Tree,\n\tlastCheckpointTree *object.Tree,\n\tworktreeFiles map[string]string,\n\tcheckpointNumber int,\n) PromptAttribution {\n\tresult := PromptAttribution{\n\t\tCheckpointNumber: checkpointNumber,\n\t}\n\n\tif len(worktreeFiles) == 0 {\n\t\treturn result\n\t}\n\n\t// Determine reference tree for user changes (last checkpoint or base)\n\treferenceTree := lastCheckpointTree\n\tif referenceTree == nil {\n\t\treferenceTree = baseTree\n\t}\n\n\tfor filePath, worktreeContent := range worktreeFiles {\n\t\treferenceContent := getFileContent(referenceTree, filePath)\n\t\tbaseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)\n\n\t\t// User changes: diff(reference, worktree)\n\t\t// These are changes since the last checkpoint that the agent didn't make\n\t\t_, userAdded, userRemoved := diffLines(referenceContent, worktreeContent)\n\t\tresult.UserLinesAdded += userAdded\n\t\tresult.UserLinesRemoved += userRemoved\n\n\t\t// Agent lines so far: diff(base, lastCheckpoint)\n\t\t// Only calculate if we have a previous checkpoint\n\t\tif lastCheckpointTree != nil {\n\t\t\tcheckpointContent := getFileContent(lastCheckpointTree, filePath)\n\t\t\t_, agentAdded, agentRemoved := diffLines(baseContent, checkpointContent)\n\t\t\tresult.AgentLinesAdded += agentAdded\n\t\t\tresult.AgentLinesRemoved += agentRemoved\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn result\n}"

err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to delete branch %s: %w\", branchName, err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// calculatePromptAttributionForSave calculates attribution at the start of a checkpoint save.\n// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent's changes are saved.\nfunc (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionForSave(\n\trepo *git.Repository,\n\tstate *SessionState,\n\tctx SaveContext,\n) PromptAttribution {\n\tnextCheckpointNum := state.CheckpointCount + 1\n\n\t// Get base tree (the commit when session started)\n\tvar baseTree *object.Tree\n\tif baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {\n\t\t\tif commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash()); err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tlastCheckpointTree, _ = commit.Tree()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Build worktree files map from the files being saved\n\t// We need to read the current content of these files\n\tworktreeFiles := make(map[string]string)\n\tworktree, err := repo.Worktree()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\t// Can't access worktree, return empty attribution\n\t\treturn PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}\n\t}\n\n\t// Get worktree root path\n\tworktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()\n\n\t// Read content of modified and new files\n\tallFiles := append(ctx.ModifiedFiles, ctx.NewFiles...)\n\tfor _, filePath := range allFiles {\n\t\tfullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)\n\t\tcontent, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue // Skip files we can't read\n\t\t}\n\t\tworktreeFiles[filePath] = string(content)\n\t}\n\n\t// Also include deleted files with empty content (so we can track removals)\n\tfor _, filePath := range ctx.DeletedFiles {\n\t\tworktreeFiles[filePath] = \"\"\n\t}\n\n\treturn CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, worktreeFiles, nextCheckpointNum)\n}"

  "new_string": "// CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated computes final attribution using accumulated prompt data.\n// This provides more accurate attribution than tree-only comparison because it captures\n// user edits that happened between checkpoints (which would otherwise be mixed into the\n// checkpoint snapshots).\n//\n// The calculation:\n// 1. Sum user edits from PromptAttributions (captured at each prompt start)\n// 2. Add user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head diff)\n// 3. Calculate agent lines from base → shadow\n// 4. Compute percentages\nfunc CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(\n\tbaseTree *object.Tree,\n\tshadowTree *object.Tree,\n\theadTree *object.Tree,\n\tfilesTouched []string,\n\tpromptAttributions []PromptAttribution,\n) *checkpoint.InitialAttribution {\n\tif len(filesTouched) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Sum accumulated user lines from prompt attributions\n\tvar accumulatedUserAdded, accumulatedUserRemoved int\n\tfor _, pa := range promptAttributions {\n\t\taccumulatedUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded\n\t\taccumulatedUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved\n\t}\n\n\t// Calculate user edits AFTER the final checkpoint (shadow → head)\n\t// These are edits the user made after the last agent checkpoint\n\tvar postCheckpointUserAdded, postCheckpointUserRemoved int\n\tvar totalAgentAdded, totalAgentRemoved int\n\n\tfor _, filePath := range filesTouched {\n\t\tbaseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)\n\t\tshadowContent := getFileContent(shadowTree, filePath)\n\t\theadContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)\n\n\t\t// Agent contribution: base → shadow\n\t\t_, agentAdded, agentRemoved := diffLines(baseContent, shadowContent)\n\t\ttotalAgentAdded += agentAdded\n\t\ttotalAgentRemoved += agentRemoved\n\n\t\t// Post-checkpoint user edits: shadow → head\n\t\t_, postUserAdded, postUserRemoved := diffLines(shadowContent, headContent)\n\t\tpostCheckpointUserAdded += postUserAdded\n\t\tpostCheckpointUserRemoved += postUserRemoved\n\t}\n\n\t// Total user contribution = accumulated (between checkpoints) + post-checkpoint\n\ttotalUserAdded := accumulatedUserAdded + postCheckpointUserAdded\n\ttotalUserRemoved := accumulatedUserRemoved + postCheckpointUserRemoved\n\n\t// Estimate modified lines (user changed existing agent lines)\n\thumanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)\n\tpureUserAdded := totalUserAdded - humanModified\n\tpureUserRemoved := totalUserRemoved - humanModified\n\n\t// Total lines in commit = agent added + user added (net new lines)\n\ttotalCommitted := totalAgentAdded + pureUserAdded\n\tif totalCommitted == 0 {\n\t\ttotalCommitted = totalAgentAdded // Fallback for delete-only\n\t}\n\n\t// Calculate percentage\n\tvar agentPercentage float64\n\tif totalCommitted > 0 {\n\t\tagentPercentage = float64(totalAgentAdded) / float64(totalCommitted) * 100\n\t}\n\n\treturn &checkpoint.InitialAttribution{\n\t\tCalculatedAt:    time.Now(),\n\t\tAgentLines:      totalAgentAdded,\n\t\tHumanAdded:      pureUserAdded,\n\t\tHumanModified:   humanModified,\n\t\tHumanRemoved:    pureUserRemoved,\n\t\tTotalCommitted:  totalCommitted,\n\t\tAgentPercentage: agentPercentage,\n\t}\n}\n\n// CalculatePromptAttribution computes line-level attribution at the start of a prompt."
}

> AGENT

I see the issue. The prompt attribution is being calculated AFTER the agent made changes, so it's counting agent changes as user changes. The calculation needs to exclude files the agent is about to save.

Let me fix the logic - the user changes should only be for files that changed but are NOT in the agent's save context.

  "new_string": "// calculatePromptAttributionForSave calculates attribution at checkpoint save time.\n// This detects user edits since the last checkpoint for files the agent is NOT touching.\n//\n// The key insight: at SaveChanges time, the worktree contains agent's changes mixed with\n// any user edits. We separate them by:\n// 1. Files in ctx.ModifiedFiles/NewFiles/DeletedFiles = agent is touching these\n// 2. Other files that changed since last checkpoint = user edits between prompts\n//\n// For files the agent IS touching, we can't distinguish user edits made before the agent\n// worked (the worktree has both mixed). Those will be detected by the final attribution\n// at commit time (shadow → committed diff).\nfunc (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionForSave(\n\trepo *git.Repository,\n\tstate *SessionState,\n\tctx SaveContext,\n) PromptAttribution {\n\tnextCheckpointNum := state.CheckpointCount + 1\n\n\t// Get base tree (the commit when session started)\n\tvar baseTree *object.Tree\n\tif baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {\n\t\tbaseTree, _ = baseCommit.Tree()\n\t}\n\n\t// Get last checkpoint tree (shadow branch, if exists)\n\tvar lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree\n\tif state.CheckpointCount > 0 {\n\t\tshadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)\n\t\trefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)\n\t\tif ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true); err == nil {\n\t\t\tif commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash()); err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tlastCheckpointTree, _ = commit.Tree()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tworktree, err := repo.Worktree()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}\n\t}\n\n\t// Build set of files the agent is touching in this checkpoint\n\tagentFiles := make(map[string]bool)\n\tfor _, f := range ctx.ModifiedFiles {\n\t\tagentFiles[f] = true\n\t}\n\tfor _, f := range ctx.NewFiles {\n\t\tagentFiles[f] = true\n\t}\n\tfor _, f := range ctx.DeletedFiles {\n\t\tagentFiles[f] = true\n\t}\n\n\t// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files\n\tstatus, err := worktree.Status()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}\n\t}\n\n\tworktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()\n\n\t// Build map of user-changed files (files that changed but agent is NOT touching)\n\tuserFiles := make(map[string]string)\n\tfor filePath, fileStatus := range status {\n\t\t// Skip files the agent is touching\n\t\tif agentFiles[filePath] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Skip unmodified files\n\t\tif fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\t// This file changed but agent isn't touching it = user edit\n\t\tfullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)\n\t\tcontent, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tuserFiles[filePath] = \"\" // File deleted or unreadable\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tuserFiles[filePath] = string(content)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Also check files in state.FilesTouched that might have been edited by user\n\t// These are files the agent touched in previous checkpoints that user might have edited\n\tfor _, filePath := range state.FilesTouched {\n\t\tif agentFiles[filePath] {\n\t\t\tcontinue // Agent touching it this checkpoint\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, already := userFiles[filePath]; already {\n\t\t\tcontinue // Already detected\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Check if this file changed since last checkpoint\n\t\treferenceTree := lastCheckpointTree\n\t\tif referenceTree == nil {\n\t\t\treferenceTree = baseTree\n\t\t}\n\t\treferenceContent := getFileContentFromTree(referenceTree, filePath)\n\t\tfullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)\n\t\tcontent, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath)\n\t\tcurrentContent := \"\"\n\t\tif err == nil {\n\t\t\tcurrentContent = string(content)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif currentContent != referenceContent {\n\t\t\tuserFiles[filePath] = currentContent\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, userFiles, nextCheckpointNum)\n}\n\n// getFileContentFromTree retrieves file content from a git tree.\nfunc getFileContentFromTree(tree *object.Tree, path string) string {\n\tif tree == nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tfile, err := tree.File(path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tcontent, err := file.Contents()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\treturn content\n}"

> AGENT

Done! Here's a summary of what was implemented:

## Summary

**Problem:** User edits made between agent checkpoints were being incorrectly attributed to the agent because checkpoint snapshots captured the full worktree state.

**Solution:** Track user/agent lines at each checkpoint save time and use accumulated data for final attribution.

### Changes Made

1. **Added `PromptAttribution` struct** (`session/state.go`, `strategy/manual_commit_types.go`):
   - Tracks `UserLinesAdded`, `UserLinesRemoved`, `AgentLinesAdded`, `AgentLinesRemoved` per checkpoint

2. **Calculate attribution at checkpoint save** (`manual_commit_git.go`):
   - `calculatePromptAttributionForSave()` detects user edits to files the agent is NOT touching
   - Excludes `.entire/` metadata directory from attribution
   - Stored in `SessionState.PromptAttributions`

3. **Use accumulated data at commit time** (`manual_commit_attribution.go`):
   - `CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated()` combines:
     - Accumulated user edits from `PromptAttributions`
     - Post-checkpoint user edits (shadow → head diff)
   - More accurate attribution than tree-only comparison

4. **Integration test** (`manual_commit_test.go`):
   - `TestMultiCheckpoint_UserEditsBetweenCheckpoints` verifies:
     - User edits different file than agent → detected at checkpoint time
     - Attribution correctly separates agent (agent.go) vs user (user.go) contributions

### Limitation
User edits to the **same file** the agent is touching in the same checkpoint cannot be separated (both are in the worktree when checkpoint saves). These are detected at commit time via shadow→head diff.

Can we add logging?

> AGENT

The comment refers to the multi-session merge scenario we discussed earlier. Here's what it means:

**Scenario:** Two sessions work on the same base commit, then user commits once.

```
Session 1: makes changes → checkpoints on shadow branch entire/<base>
Session 2: makes changes → checkpoints on SAME shadow branch entire/<base>
User commits → both sessions condense
```

**Why keep the first session's attribution:**

1. Both sessions share the **same shadow branch** (because they have the same base commit)
2. The shadow branch contains **all agent work from both sessions** combined
3. When Session 1 condenses first, it calculates attribution comparing:
   - `base → shadow` (all agent work)
   - `shadow → head` (user edits after final checkpoint)
4. When Session 2 condenses, it would calculate the **same** comparison since the trees are identical

So we skip recalculating because the result would be the same.

**However**, the comment is slightly incomplete now with the `PromptAttribution` tracking - Session 1's accumulated `PromptAttributions` might differ from Session 2's (tracking different user edits between their respective checkpoints). But since both sessions' agent work is on the same shadow branch, the tree comparison is still valid.

Would you like me to update the comment to be more precise?

> DEVELOPER

got this feedback: 

The calculation of actualHumanRemoved has a potential logic issue. The current approach tries to infer human removals by subtracting agent removals from total commit removals. However, this doesn't correctly handle the case where the agent added lines that the human then removed.

Example scenario:

Agent adds "lineA" and "lineB" (2 new lines)
Human removes "lineB" (1 line)
Result: base → committed shows +1 line (lineA)
In this case:

commitRemoved = 0 (base → committed shows no removals, just additions)
humanRemoved (checkpoint → committed) = 1 (lineB was removed)
agentRemovedFromBase = 0 (agent added lines, didn't remove)
actualHumanRemoved = 0 - 0 = 0 (incorrect, should be 1)
The capping at line 73-75 tries to fix this by limiting to pureHumanRemoved, but the condition actualHumanRemoved > pureHumanRemoved is false (0 > 1), so the cap doesn't apply.

Consider simplifying this to use pureHumanRemoved directly, or add a test case to verify this scenario works correctly. Note: CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated is the primary function used in manual-commit condensation, so this may not be exercised in practice, but the function is exported and could be used elsewhere.

Good catch. Let me trace through the example to understand the issue:

**Scenario:** Agent adds "lineA" and "lineB", human removes "lineB"

```
base = ""
checkpoint = "lineA\nlineB\n"  
committed = "lineA\n"
```

**Current calculation:**
- `commitRemoved` = 0 (base → committed: nothing removed from base)
- `humanRemoved` = 1 (checkpoint → committed: lineB removed)
- `pureHumanRemoved` = 1
- `agentRemovedFromBase` = 0 - 2 = -2 → clamped to 0
- `actualHumanRemoved` = 0 - 0 = 0 ❌ (should be 1)

The issue is that `commitRemoved` doesn't capture lines the agent added that were then removed by the human, because those lines weren't in base.

The fix is simple: `pureHumanRemoved` already has the right value from `diffLines(checkpoint, committed)`.

You're right, let me re-examine this.

The **ideal** approach: at the actual start of a prompt (before the agent runs), compare worktree to last checkpoint. Any diff is purely user changes since the agent hasn't done anything yet.

The **current** implementation: we calculate during `SaveChanges()` which runs AFTER the agent has already modified the worktree. At that point, the worktree contains both user edits AND agent edits. That's why I added filtering - to exclude files the agent touched.

But this causes two problems:
1. We can't detect user edits to files the agent also modified
2. User edits to files the agent DIDN'T touch get counted in prompt attribution, but aren't saved to shadow branch, so they get counted again in shadow→head diff

The real fix should be: calculate the attribution at actual prompt start, before the agent makes any changes. Then we don't need filtering at all.

Is there a hook or event we can use to capture worktree state at prompt start, before any agent tool calls? Currently we only hook into checkpoint saves (after agent changes).

    22→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.
    23→// This works even when stdin is redirected (e.g., git commit -m).
    24→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    25→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    26→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    27→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    28→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    29→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    30→	if err != nil {
    31→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    32→		return defaultYes
    33→	}
    34→	defer tty.Close()
    35→
    36→	// Show context if provided
    37→	if context != "" {
    38→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    39→	}
    40→
    41→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    42→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    43→	var hint string
    44→	if defaultYes {
    45→		hint = "[Y/n]"
    46→	} else {
    47→		hint = "[y/N]"
    48→	}
    49→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    50→
    51→	// Read response
    52→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    53→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
    54→	if err != nil {
    55→		return defaultYes
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
    59→	switch response {
    60→	case "y", "yes":
    61→		return true
    62→	case "n", "no":
    63→		return false
    64→	default:
    65→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
    66→		return defaultYes
    67→	}
    68→}

    70→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
    71→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
    72→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
    73→//
    74→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
    75→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(commitMsgFile string) error {
    76→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
    77→	if err != nil {
    78→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
    79→	}
    80→
    81→	message := string(content)
    82→
    83→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
    84→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
    85→		// No trailer, nothing to do
    86→		return nil
    87→	}
    88→
    89→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
    90→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
    91→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
    92→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
    93→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
    94→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
    95→		}
    96→	}
    97→
    98→	return nil
    99→}
   100→
   101→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   102→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   103→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   104→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   105→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   106→		// Skip empty lines
   107→		if trimmed == "" {
   108→			continue
   109→		}
   110→		// Skip comment lines
   111→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   112→			continue
   113→		}
   114→		// Skip our trailer line
   115→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   116→			continue
   117→		}
   118→		// Found user content
   119→		return true
   120→	}
   121→	return false
   122→}
   123→
   124→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   125→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   126→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   127→	var result []string
   128→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   129→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   130→			result = append(result, line)
   131→		}
   132→	}
   133→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   134→}

   136→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   137→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   138→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   139→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   140→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   141→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   142→//
   143→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   144→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   145→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   146→//   - "merge", "squash", "commit": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated or amend commits)
   147→//
   148→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   149→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   150→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   151→
   152→	// Skip for merge, squash, and commit (amend) sources
   153→	// These are auto-generated or reusing existing messages - not from Claude sessions
   154→	switch source {
   155→	case "merge", "squash", "commit":
   156→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",
   157→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   158→			slog.String("source", source),
   159→		)
   160→		return nil
   161→	}

   163→	if err != nil {
   164→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   165→	}

   167→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   168→	if err != nil {
   169→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   173→	// We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because the user may have made
   174→	// intermediate commits without entering new prompts, causing HEAD to diverge
   175→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   176→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   177→		// No active sessions or error listing - silently skip (hooks must be resilient)
   178→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions",
   179→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   180→			slog.String("source", source),
   181→		)
   182→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   183→	}
   184→
   185→	// Check if any session has new content to condense
   186→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)

   189→	var checkpointID id.CheckpointID

   191→	var reusedSession *SessionState

   195→		hasNewContent = true
   196→	} else {

   198→		// This handles the case where user splits Claude's work across multiple commits

   200→		// - FilesTouched empty: commits made before session stop, reuse checkpoint
   201→		// - FilesTouched populated: only reuse if files overlap (prevents unrelated commits from reusing)
   202→
   203→		// Get current HEAD to filter sessions
   204→		head, err := repo.Head()
   205→		if err != nil {
   206→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   207→		}
   208→		currentHeadHash := head.Hash().String()
   209→
   210→		// Filter to sessions where BaseCommit matches current HEAD
   211→		// This prevents reusing checkpoint IDs from old sessions
   212→		// Note: BaseCommit is kept current both when new content is condensed (in the
   213→		// condensation process) and when no new content is found (via PostCommit when
   214→		// reusing checkpoint IDs). If none match, we don't add a trailer rather than
   215→		// falling back to old sessions which could have stale checkpoint IDs.
   216→		var currentSessions []*SessionState
   217→		for _, session := range sessions {
   218→			if session.BaseCommit == currentHeadHash {
   219→				currentSessions = append(currentSessions, session)
   220→			}
   221→		}
   222→
   223→		if len(currentSessions) == 0 {
   224→			// No sessions match current HEAD - don't try to reuse checkpoint IDs
   225→			// from old sessions as they may be stale
   226→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no sessions match current HEAD",
   227→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   228→				slog.String("source", source),
   229→				slog.String("current_head", currentHeadHash[:7]),
   230→				slog.Int("total_sessions", len(sessions)),
   231→			)
   232→			return nil
   233→		}
   234→
   235→		stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
   236→		for _, session := range currentSessions {
   237→			if !session.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() &&
   238→				(len(session.FilesTouched) == 0 || hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, session.FilesTouched)) {
   239→				checkpointID = session.LastCheckpointID
   240→				reusedSession = session
   241→				break
   242→			}
   243→		}
   244→		if checkpointID.IsEmpty() {
   245→			// No new content and no previous checkpoint to reference (or staged files are unrelated)
   246→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no content to link",
   247→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   248→				slog.String("source", source),
   249→				slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   250→				slog.Int("sessions_with_content", len(sessionsWithContent)),
   251→			)
   252→			return nil
   253→		}
   254→	}
   255→
   256→	// Read current commit message
   257→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   258→	if err != nil {
   259→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   260→	}
   261→
   262→	message := string(content)
   263→
   264→	// Get or generate checkpoint ID (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   265→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   266→		// Trailer already exists (e.g., amend) - keep it
   267→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer already exists",
   268→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   269→			slog.String("source", source),
   270→			slog.String("existing_checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   271→		)
   272→		return nil
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	if hasNewContent {
   276→		// New content: generate new checkpoint ID
   277→		cpID, err := id.Generate()
   278→		if err != nil {
   279→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   280→		}
   281→		checkpointID = cpID
   282→	}
   283→	// Otherwise checkpointID is already set to LastCheckpointID from above
   284→
   285→	// Determine agent type and last prompt from session
   286→	agentType := DefaultAgentType // default for backward compatibility
   287→	var lastPrompt string
   288→	if hasNewContent && len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   289→		session := sessionsWithContent[0]
   290→		if session.AgentType != "" {
   291→			agentType = session.AgentType
   292→		}
   293→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, session)
   294→	} else if reusedSession != nil {
   295→		// Reusing checkpoint from existing session - get agent type and prompt from that session
   296→		if reusedSession.AgentType != "" {
   297→			agentType = reusedSession.AgentType
   298→		}
   299→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, reusedSession)
   300→	}
   301→
   302→	// Prepare prompt for display: collapse newlines/whitespace, then truncate (rune-safe)
   303→	displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(lastPrompt), 80, "...")
   304→
   305→	// Add trailer differently based on commit source
   306→	if source == "message" {
   307→		// Using -m or -F: ask user interactively whether to add trailer
   308→		// (comments won't be stripped by git in this mode)
   309→
   310→		// Build context string for interactive prompt
   311→		var promptContext string
   312→		if displayPrompt != "" {
   313→			promptContext = "You have an active " + string(agentType) + " session.\nLast Prompt: " + displayPrompt
   314→		}
   315→
   316→		if !askConfirmTTY("Link this commit to "+string(agentType)+" session context?", promptContext, true) {
   317→			// User declined - don't add trailer
   318→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   319→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   320→				slog.String("source", source),
   321→			)
   322→			return nil
   323→		}
   324→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   325→	} else {
   326→		// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   327→		message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   331→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   332→		slog.String("source", source),
   333→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   334→		slog.Bool("has_new_content", hasNewContent),
   335→	)
   336→
   337→	// Write updated message back
   338→	if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   339→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   340→	}
   341→
   342→	return nil
   343→}
   344→
   345→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   346→// Checks if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer and if so, condenses
   347→// session data from shadow branches to entire/sessions.
   348→// If the user removed the trailer during commit message editing, this is treated
   349→// as a "manual" commit and no condensation happens.
   350→//
   351→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   352→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostCommit() error {
   353→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   354→
   355→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   356→	if err != nil {
   357→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   358→	}
   359→
   360→	// Get HEAD commit to check for trailer
   361→	head, err := repo.Head()
   362→	if err != nil {
   363→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   364→	}
   365→
   366→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   367→	if err != nil {
   368→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   369→	}
   370→
   371→	// Check if commit has checkpoint trailer (ParseCheckpoint validates format)
   372→	checkpointID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(commit.Message)
   373→	if !found {
   374→		// No trailer - user removed it, treat as manual commit
   375→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no checkpoint trailer",
   376→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   377→		)
   378→		return nil
   379→	}
   380→
   381→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   382→	if err != nil {
   383→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   384→	}
   385→
   386→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   387→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   388→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   389→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: no active sessions despite trailer",
   390→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   391→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   392→		)
   393→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   394→	}
   395→
   396→	// Filter to sessions with new content
   397→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   398→	if len(sessionsWithContent) == 0 {
   399→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no new content to condense",
   400→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   401→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   402→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   403→		)
   404→		// Still update BaseCommit for all sessions in this worktree
   405→		// This prevents stale BaseCommit when commits happen without condensation
   406→		// (e.g., when reusing a previous checkpoint ID for split commits)
   407→		newHead := head.Hash().String()
   408→		for _, state := range sessions {
   409→			if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   410→				state.BaseCommit = newHead
   411→				if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   412→					logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: failed to update session BaseCommit",
   413→						slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   414→						slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   415→					)
   416→				}
   417→			}
   418→		}
   419→		return nil
   420→	}
   421→
   422→	// Track shadow branches to clean up after successful condensation
   423→	shadowBranchesToDelete := make(map[string]struct{})
   424→
   425→	// Condense sessions that have new content
   426→	for _, state := range sessionsWithContent {
   427→		result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
   428→		if err != nil {
   429→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: condensation failed for session %s: %v\n",
   430→				state.SessionID, err)
   431→			continue
   432→		}
   433→
   434→		// Track this shadow branch for cleanup
   435→		shadowBranchesToDelete[state.BaseCommit] = struct{}{}
   436→
   437→		// Update session state for the new base commit
   438→		// After condensation, the session continues from the NEW commit (HEAD), so we:
   439→		// 1. Update BaseCommit to new HEAD - session now tracks from new commit
   440→		// 2. Reset CheckpointCount to 0 - no checkpoints exist on new shadow branch yet
   441→		// 3. Update CondensedTranscriptLines - track transcript position for detecting new content
   442→		//
   443→		// This is critical: if we don't update BaseCommit, listAllSessionStates will try
   444→		// to find shadow branch for old commit (which gets deleted), and since CheckpointCount > 0,
   445→		// it will clean up (delete) the session state file. By updating to new HEAD with
   446→		// CheckpointCount = 0, the session is preserved even without a shadow branch.
   447→		state.BaseCommit = head.Hash().String()
   448→		state.CheckpointCount = 0
   449→		state.CondensedTranscriptLines = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   450→
   451→		// Save checkpoint ID so subsequent commits without new content can reuse it
   452→		state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   453→
   454→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   455→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", err)
   456→		}
   457→
   458→		shortID := state.SessionID
   459→		if len(shortID) > 8 {
   460→			shortID = shortID[:8]
   461→		}
   462→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Condensed session %s: %s (%d checkpoints)\n",
   463→			shortID, result.CheckpointID, result.CheckpointsCount)
   464→
   465→		// Log condensation
   466→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   467→		logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed",
   468→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   469→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   470→			slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   471→			slog.Int("transcript_lines", result.TotalTranscriptLines),
   472→		)
   473→	}
   474→
   475→	// Clean up shadow branches after successful condensation
   476→	// Data is now preserved on entire/sessions, so shadow branches are no longer needed
   477→	for baseCommit := range shadowBranchesToDelete {
   478→		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit)
   479→		if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
   480→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to clean up %s: %v\n", shadowBranchName, err)
   481→		} else {
   482→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Cleaned up shadow branch: %s\n", shadowBranchName)
   483→
   484→			// Log branch cleanup
   485→			logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   486→			logging.Info(logCtx, "shadow branch deleted",
   487→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   488→				slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   489→			)
   490→		}
   491→	}
   492→
   493→	return nil
   494→}
   495→
   496→// filterSessionsWithNewContent returns sessions that have new transcript content
   497→// beyond what was already condensed.
   498→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo *git.Repository, sessions []*SessionState) []*SessionState {
   499→	var result []*SessionState
   500→
   501→	for _, state := range sessions {
   502→		hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
   503→		if err != nil {
   504→			// On error, include the session (fail open for hooks)
   505→			result = append(result, state)
   506→			continue
   507→		}
   508→		if hasNew {
   509→			result = append(result, state)
   510→		}
   511→	}
   512→
   513→	return result
   514→}
   515→
   516→// sessionHasNewContent checks if a session has new transcript content
   517→// beyond what was already condensed.
   518→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   519→	// Get shadow branch
   520→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit)
   521→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   522→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   523→	if err != nil {
   524→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   525→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   526→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.
   527→		return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
   528→	}
   529→
   530→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   531→	if err != nil {
   532→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   533→	}
   534→
   535→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   536→	if err != nil {
   537→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   538→	}
   539→
   540→	// Look for transcript file
   541→	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
   542→	var transcriptLines int
   543→
   544→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   545→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   546→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   547→		}
   548→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   549→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   550→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   551→		}
   552→	}
   553→
   554→	// Has new content if there are more lines than already condensed
   555→	return transcriptLines > state.CondensedTranscriptLines, nil
   556→}
   557→
   558→// countTranscriptLines counts lines in a transcript, matching the counting method used
   559→// in extractSessionData for consistency. This trims trailing empty lines (from final \n
   560→// in JSONL) but includes empty lines in the middle of the file.
   561→func countTranscriptLines(content string) int {
   562→	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   563→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   564→	for len(lines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[len(lines)-1]) == "" {
   565→		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1]
   566→	}
   567→	return len(lines)
   568→}
   569→
   570→// sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript checks if a session has new content
   571→// by examining the live transcript file. This is used when no shadow branch exists
   572→// (i.e., no Stop has happened yet) but the agent may have done work.
   573→//
   574→// Returns true if:
   575→//  1. The transcript has grown since the last condensation, AND
   576→//  2. The new transcript portion contains file modifications, AND
   577→//  3. At least one modified file overlaps with the currently staged files
   578→//
   579→// The overlap check ensures we don't add checkpoint trailers to commits that are
   580→// unrelated to the agent's recent changes.
   581→//
   582→// This handles the scenario where the agent commits mid-session before Stop.
   583→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   584→	// Need both transcript path and agent type to analyze
   585→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" || state.AgentType == "" {
   586→		return false, nil
   587→	}
   588→
   589→	// Get the agent for transcript analysis
   590→	ag, err := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType)
   591→	if err != nil {
   592→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Unknown agent type, fail gracefully
   593→	}
   594→
   595→	// Cast to TranscriptAnalyzer
   596→	analyzer, ok := ag.(agent.TranscriptAnalyzer)
   597→	if !ok {
   598→		return false, nil // Agent doesn't support transcript analysis
   599→	}
   600→
   601→	// Get current transcript position
   602→	currentPos, err := analyzer.GetTranscriptPosition(state.TranscriptPath)
   603→	if err != nil {
   604→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error reading transcript, fail gracefully
   605→	}
   606→
   607→	// Check if transcript has grown since last condensation
   608→	if currentPos <= state.CondensedTranscriptLines {
   609→		return false, nil // No new content
   610→	}
   611→
   612→	// Transcript has grown - check if there are file modifications in the new portion
   613→	modifiedFiles, _, err := analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(state.TranscriptPath, state.CondensedTranscriptLines)
   614→	if err != nil {
   615→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error parsing transcript, fail gracefully
   616→	}
   617→
   618→	// No file modifications means no new content to checkpoint
   619→	if len(modifiedFiles) == 0 {
   620→		return false, nil
   621→	}
   622→
   623→	// Check if any modified files overlap with currently staged files
   624→	// This ensures we only add checkpoint trailers to commits that include
   625→	// files the agent actually modified
   626→	stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo)
   627→	if !hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, modifiedFiles) {
   628→		return false, nil // No overlap - staged files are unrelated to agent's work
   629→	}
   630→
   631→	return true, nil
   632→}
   633→
   634→// addCheckpointTrailer adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer to a commit message.
   635→// Handles proper trailer formatting (blank line before trailers if needed).
   636→func addCheckpointTrailer(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) string {
   637→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   638→
   639→	// If message already ends with trailers (lines starting with key:), just append
   640→	// Otherwise, add a blank line first
   641→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), "\n")
   642→
   643→	// Check if last non-empty, non-comment line looks like a trailer
   644→	// Git comment lines start with # and may contain ": " (e.g., "# Changes to be committed:")
   645→	hasTrailers := false
   646→	for i := len(lines) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   647→		line := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   648→		if line == "" {
   649→			break
   650→		}
   651→		// Skip git comment lines
   652→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   653→			continue
   654→		}
   655→		if strings.Contains(line, ": ") {
   656→			hasTrailers = true
   657→			break
   658→		}
   659→		// Non-comment, non-trailer line found - no existing trailers
   660→		break
   661→	}
   662→
   663→	if hasTrailers {
   664→		// Append trailer directly
   665→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n" + trailer + "\n"
   666→	}
   667→
   668→	// Add blank line before trailer
   669→	return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n"
   670→}
   671→
   672→// addCheckpointTrailerWithComment adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer with an explanatory comment.
   673→// The trailer is placed above the git comment block but below the user's message area,
   674→// with a comment explaining that the user can remove it if they don't want to link the commit
   675→// to the agent session. If prompt is non-empty, it's shown as context.
   676→func addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, agentName, prompt string) string {
   677→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   678→	commentLines := []string{
   679→		"# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link this commit to " + agentName + " session context.",
   680→	}
   681→	if prompt != "" {
   682→		commentLines = append(commentLines, "# Last Prompt: "+prompt)
   683→	}
   684→	commentLines = append(commentLines, "# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.")
   685→	comment := strings.Join(commentLines, "\n")
   686→
   687→	lines := strings.Split(message, "\n")
   688→
   689→	// Find where the git comment block starts (first # line)
   690→	commentStart := -1
   691→	for i, line := range lines {
   692→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   693→			commentStart = i
   694→			break
   695→		}
   696→	}
   697→
   698→	if commentStart == -1 {
   699→		// No git comments, append trailer at the end
   700→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n"
   701→	}
   702→
   703→	// Split into user content and git comments
   704→	userContent := strings.Join(lines[:commentStart], "\n")
   705→	gitComments := strings.Join(lines[commentStart:], "\n")
   706→
   707→	// Build result: user content, blank line, trailer, comment, blank line, git comments
   708→	userContent = strings.TrimRight(userContent, "\n")
   709→	if userContent == "" {
   710→		// No user content yet - leave space for them to type, then trailer
   711→		// Two newlines: first for user's message line, second for blank separator
   712→		return "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   713→	}
   714→	return userContent + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   715→}
   716→
   717→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
   718→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.
   719→// Called during UserPromptSubmit to allow git hooks to detect active sessions.
   720→//
   721→// If the session already exists and HEAD has moved (e.g., user committed), updates
   722→// BaseCommit to the new HEAD so future checkpoints go to the correct shadow branch.
   723→//
   724→// If there's an existing shadow branch with activity from a different worktree,
   725→// returns a ShadowBranchConflictError to allow the caller to inform the user.
   726→//
   727→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
   728→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
   729→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string) error {
   730→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   731→	if err != nil {
   732→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   733→	}
   734→
   735→	// Get current HEAD
   736→	head, err := repo.Head()
   737→	if err != nil {
   738→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   739→	}
   740→
   741→	// Check if session already exists
   742→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   743→	if err != nil {
   744→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check session state: %w", err)
   745→	}
   746→
   747→	// Check for shadow branch conflict before proceeding
   748→	// This must happen even if session state exists but has no checkpoints yet
   749→	// (e.g., state was created by concurrent warning but conflict later resolved)
   750→	baseCommitHash := head.Hash().String()
   751→	if state == nil || state.CheckpointCount == 0 {
   752→		shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommitHash)
   753→		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranch)
   754→
   755→		ref, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   756→		if refErr == nil {
   757→			// Shadow branch exists - check if it has commits from a different session
   758→			tipCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   759→			if commitErr == nil {
   760→				existingSessionID, found := trailers.ParseSession(tipCommit.Message)
   761→				if found && existingSessionID != sessionID {
   762→					// Check if the existing session has a state file
   763→					// existingSessionID is the full Entire session ID (YYYY-MM-DD-uuid) from the trailer
   764→					// We intentionally ignore load errors - treat them as "no state" (orphaned branch)
   765→					existingState, _ := s.loadSessionState(existingSessionID) //nolint:errcheck // error means no state
   766→					if existingState == nil {
   767→						// Orphaned shadow branch - no state file for the existing session
   768→						// Reset the branch so the new session can proceed
   769→						fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Resetting orphaned shadow branch '%s' (previous session %s has no state)\n",
   770→							shadowBranch, existingSessionID)
   771→						if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranch); err != nil {
   772→							return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset orphaned shadow branch: %w", err)
   773→						}
   774→					} else {
   775→						// Existing session has state - this is a real conflict
   776→						// (e.g., different worktree at same commit)
   777→						return &SessionIDConflictError{
   778→							ExistingSession: existingSessionID,
   779→							NewSession:      sessionID,
   780→							ShadowBranch:    shadowBranch,
   781→						}
   782→					}
   783→				}
   784→			}
   785→		}
   786→	}
   787→
   788→	if state != nil && state.BaseCommit != "" {
   789→		// Session is fully initialized
   790→		needSave := false
   791→
   792→		// Backfill AgentType if empty (for sessions created before the agent_type field was added)
   793→		if state.AgentType == "" && agentType != "" {
   794→			state.AgentType = agentType
   795→			needSave = true
   796→		}
   797→
   798→		// Update transcript path if provided (may change on session resume)
   799→		if transcriptPath != "" && state.TranscriptPath != transcriptPath {
   800→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath

   802→		}
   803→
   804→		// Clear LastCheckpointID on every new prompt
   805→		// This is set during PostCommit when a checkpoint is created, and should be
   806→		// cleared when the user enters a new prompt (starting fresh work)
   807→		if state.LastCheckpointID != "" {
   808→			state.LastCheckpointID = ""
   809→			needSave = true
   810→		}
   811→

   813→		if state.BaseCommit != head.Hash().String() {
   814→			oldBaseCommit := state.BaseCommit
   815→			newBaseCommit := head.Hash().String()
   816→
   817→			// Check if old shadow branch exists - if so, user did NOT commit (would have been deleted)
   818→			// This happens when user does: stash → pull → stash apply, or rebase, etc.
   819→			oldShadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(oldBaseCommit)
   820→			oldRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(oldShadowBranch)
   821→			if oldRef, err := repo.Reference(oldRefName, true); err == nil {
   822→				// Old shadow branch exists - move it to new base commit
   823→				newShadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(newBaseCommit)
   824→				newRefName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(newShadowBranch)
   825→
   826→				// Create new reference pointing to same commit
   827→				newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(newRefName, oldRef.Hash())
   828→				if err := repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
   829→					return fmt.Errorf("failed to create new shadow branch %s: %w", newShadowBranch, err)
   830→				}
   831→
   832→				// Delete old reference
   833→				if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(oldRefName); err != nil {
   834→					// Non-fatal: log but continue
   835→					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to remove old shadow branch %s: %v\n", oldShadowBranch, err)
   836→				}
   837→
   838→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Moved shadow branch from %s to %s (base commit changed after pull/rebase)\n",
   839→					oldShadowBranch, newShadowBranch)
   840→			}
   841→
   842→			state.BaseCommit = newBaseCommit
   843→			needSave = true
   844→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Updated session base commit to %s\n", newBaseCommit[:7])
   845→		}
   846→
   847→		if needSave {

   849→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
   850→			}
   851→		}
   852→		return nil
   853→	}
   854→	// If state exists but BaseCommit is empty, it's a partial state from concurrent warning
   855→	// Continue below to properly initialize it

   858→	if err != nil {

   866→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to check for existing sessions: %v\n", err)

   870→			if existingState.WorktreePath == currentWorktree {

   872→			}
   873→
   874→			// Found a session from a different worktree on the same base commit
   875→			shadowBranch := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(head.Hash().String())

   883→			}
   884→		}
   885→	}

   891→	}
   892→
   893→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Initialized shadow session: %s\n", sessionID)
   894→	return nil
   895→}
